## 35. Round Table Conference

**Q1.** Which of the following Indian leaders attended the First Round Table Conference in London?

- **A.** Maulana Mohammad Ali
- **B.** Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
- **C.** Mahatma Gandhi
- **D.** Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru

**Answer:** A — Maulana Mohammad Ali
**Explanation:** The report of the Simon Commission was published on 10th June and 24th June, 1930. Political organizations had refused the recommendations of Commission. Main leaders of Congress were in jails. British Government organized 1st Round Table Conference on November, 1930 to January 1931 in London in the environment of frustration and dissatisfaction. 89 Indian delegates members participated in 1st Round Table Conference, but Congress did not participate. Main participants of 1st Round Table Conference were: Tej Bahadur Sapru, Srinivas Shastri, Muhammad Ali, Muhammad Shafi, Aga Khan III, Fazlul Haq, Muhammad Ali Jinnah, Homi Mody, M. R. Jaykar, Dr. B. S. Moonje, Bhimrao Ambedkar and Sundar Singh Majithia, etc.
*Asked in:* 44th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2000

**Q2.** Which one of the following is not true about the First Round Table Conference?

- **A.** It was held in 1930
- **B.** It was to discuss the Report of the Simon Commission
- **C.** It was held in London
- **D.** It was attended by the Congress delegation.

**Answer:** D — It was attended by the Congress delegation.
**Explanation:** The report of the Simon Commission was published on 10th June and 24th June, 1930. Political organizations had refused the recommendations of Commission. Main leaders of Congress were in jails. British Government organized 1st Round Table Conference on November, 1930 to January 1931 in London in the environment of frustration and dissatisfaction. 89 Indian delegates members participated in 1st Round Table Conference, but Congress did not participate. Main participants of 1st Round Table Conference were: Tej Bahadur Sapru, Srinivas Shastri, Muhammad Ali, Muhammad Shafi, Aga Khan III, Fazlul Haq, Muhammad Ali Jinnah, Homi Mody, M. R. Jaykar, Dr. B. S. Moonje, Bhimrao Ambedkar and Sundar Singh Majithia, etc.
*Asked in:* U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2010

**Q22.** The meeting of Indian and British political leaders during 1930-32 in London has often been referred to as the First, Second and Third Round Table Conferences. It would be incorrect to refer to them as such because:

- **A.** The Indian National Congress did not take part in two of them

- **C.** The British Labour Party had withdrawn from the Conference making the proceedings of the Conference partisan
- **D.** It was an instance of a Conference held in three sessions and not that of three separate, conference

**Answer:** D — It was an instance of a Conference held in three sessions and not that of three separate, conference
**Explanation:** First, Second and Third Round Table Conferences were not three separate conferences; ideally, they were three sessions of a single Conference. It would be wrong to call three sessions of a single Conference three separate Conferences. The main objective of the Round Table Conference was to discuss the Simon Commission Report and improvisation of the political situation.

## 36. Communal Award And Poona Pact (1932)

**Q1.** Who among the following issued the 'Communal Award'?

- **A.** Ramsay Macdonald
- **B.** Stanley Baldwin
- **C.** Neville Chamberlain
- **D.** Winston Churchill

**Answer:** A — Ramsay Macdonald
**Explanation:** No consensus was made on the subject of separate electorate for Depressed Classes and various communities in Second Round Table Conference. The His Majesty Government's declared position (endorsed by Parliament) that if communities failed to agree the government would devise and apply a scheme. As a result British PM Ramsay MacDonald found a solution. Accordingly, Ramsay Macdonald declared his "Communal Award" on 16 Aug. 1932 A. D.
*Asked in:* U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1999

**Q2.** A separate electoral group was made by the communal Tribunal of Ramsay MacDonald first time in August, 1932-

- **A.** for Muslims
- **B.** for Indian Christians
- **C.** for Anglo-Indians
- **D.** for Untouchables

**Answer:** D — for Untouchables
**Explanation:** British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald announced Communal Award on 16 August 1932 A. D. According to Legislative Assembly provisions, few seats of Legislative Assembly were reserved for minorities whose candidates were to be elected by separate electorates members of the depressed classes qualified to vote, will vote in a general constituency and they are also entitled to vote in a general constituency. Muslims and Sikhs were already considered minorities (although Europeans, Anglo-Indians, Indian Christians were provided with separate electorates in 1919). Now the Depressed Classes (untouchables) were to be declared minorities as per provisions of the new law.
*Asked in:* 42nd B.P.S.C. (Pre) 1997

**Q3.** Consider the statements : Assertion (A) : The British Government announced the Communal Award in August 1932. Reason (R) : It allowed to each minority a number of seats in the legislature to be elected on the basis of a separate electorate. Select the correct answer using the codes given below:

- **A.** Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
- **B.** Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
- **C.** (A) is true, but (R) is false.
- **D.** (A) is false, but (R) is true.

**Answer:** A — Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
**Explanation:** British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald announced Communal Award on 16 August 1932 A. D. According to Legislative Assembly provisions, few seats of Legislative Assembly were reserved for minorities whose candidates were to be elected by separate electorates members of the depressed classes qualified to vote, will vote in a general constituency and they are also entitled to vote in a general constituency. Muslims and Sikhs were already considered minorities (although Europeans, Anglo-Indians, Indian Christians were provided with separate electorates in 1919). Now the Depressed Classes (untouchables) were to be declared minorities as per provisions of the new law.
*Asked in:* U.P.R.O. /A.R.O. (Mains) 2017

**Q4.** Which were not allocated separate electorates and reserved seats by Communal Award of MacDonald?

- **A.** Muslims
- **B.** Sikhs
- **C.** Depressed Classes
- **D.** Buddhists

**Answer:** D — Buddhists
**Explanation:** British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald announced Communal Award on August 16, 1932 A. D. in which th separate electorates were granted not only to Muslims but also to Depressed Classes. In addition to this Indian Christians, Sikhs, Anglo-Indians and others were granted the separate electorates which were applicable only to provincial Legislative Assemblies. Hence, it is clear that Buddhists were not granted separate electorates.
*Asked in:* U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2001

**Q5.** When did Mahatma Gandhi start first fast unto death?

- **A.** At the time of Communal Award
- **B.** At the time of Calcutta Riots
- **C.** At the time of Jallianwala Bagh Mishap.
- **D.** At the time of Delhi Riots

**Answer:** A — At the time of Communal Award
**Explanation:** On September 20, 1932 A. D., Mahatma Gandhi began his first fast unto death in Yerwada Jail to protest Communal Award of British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald. On 24 September, 1932 A. D. Poona Pact was signed between followers of Gandhi and B. R. Ambedkar. After that it was given approved and fast ended on 26 September, 1932 A. D.
*Asked in:* Uttarakhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2010

- **C.** Yerwada Jail
- **D.** None of the above

**Answer:** C — Yerwada Jail
**Explanation:** On September 20, 1932 A. D., Mahatma Gandhi began his first fast unto death in Yerwada Jail to protest Communal Award of British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald. On 24 September, 1932 A. D. Poona Pact was signed between followers of Gandhi and B. R. Ambedkar. After that it was given approved and fast ended on 26 September, 1932 A. D.
*Asked in:* Chhattisgarh P.C.S. (Pre) 2022

**Answer:** C — Ramsay MacDonald announced the Communal Award
**Explanation:** On September 20, 1932 A. D., Mahatma Gandhi began his first fast unto death in Yerwada Jail to protest Communal Award of British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald. On 24 September, 1932 A. D. Poona Pact was signed between followers of Gandhi and B. R. Ambedkar. After that it was given approved and fast ended on 26 September, 1932 A. D.
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 2012

**Q8.** How many seats were given to depressed classes under Communal Award and Poona Pact?

- **A.** 74 and 79 respectively
- **B.** 71 and 147 respectively
- **C.** 78 and 80 respectively
- **D.** 78 and 69 respectively

**Answer:** B — 71 and 147 respectively
**Explanation:** The number of reserved seats for depressed classes in Provincial Legislatures were 71 in Communal Award which was increased to 148 by Poona Pact (Madras =30, Sindh with Bombay = 15, Punjab = 8, Bihar and Odisha = 18, Central Provinces = 20, Assam= 7, Bengal = 30, United Provinces= 20). Though, some books mention that there are 147 seats. In addition to this, 18% seats in General class seats were reserved for depressed class in Central Legislature.
*Asked in:* 47th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2005

**Q9.** The Poona Pact was concerned with:

- **A.** Depressed classes
- **B.** Hindu-Muslim unity
- **C.** Constitutional progress
- **D.** Educational reforms

**Answer:** A — Depressed classes
**Explanation:** The number of reserved seats for depressed classes in Provincial Legislatures were 71 in Communal Award which was increased to 148 by Poona Pact (Madras =30, Sindh with Bombay = 15, Punjab = 8, Bihar and Odisha = 18, Central Provinces = 20, Assam= 7, Bengal = 30, United Provinces= 20). Though, some books mention that there are 147 seats. In addition to this, 18% seats in General class seats were reserved for depressed class in Central Legislature.
*Asked in:* U.P. Lower Sub. (Pre) 2008; U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2007; U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1996

**Q10.** The purpose of Poona Pact was:

- **A.** Hindu-Muslim unity
- **B.** To provide representation of untouchables
- **C.** To privileged the Kings
- **D.** Reconsideration of Dyarchy

**Answer:** B — To provide representation of untouchables
**Explanation:** The number of reserved seats for depressed classes in Provincial Legislatures were 71 in Communal Award which was increased to 148 by Poona Pact (Madras =30, Sindh with Bombay = 15, Punjab = 8, Bihar and Odisha = 18, Central Provinces = 20, Assam= 7, Bengal = 30, United Provinces= 20). Though, some books mention that there are 147 seats. In addition to this, 18% seats in General class seats were reserved for depressed class in Central Legislature.
*Asked in:* U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 1997; 46th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2004

**Q11.** Assertion (A) : The Poona Pact defeated the purpose of Communal Award. Reason (R) : It paved the way for reservation of seats in the Parliament and the State Assemblies for the SC and ST people. Select the correct answer from the code given below: Code :

- **A.** Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
- **B.** Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not a correct explanation of (A).
- **C.** (A) is true, but (R) is false.
- **D.** (A) is false, but (R) is true.

**Answer:** A — Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
**Explanation:** On 16 August, 1932 A. D., Ramsay Macdonald announced his Communal Award. The award authorised Indian Christians, Muslims, Europeans, Sikhs, Depressed Classes and others to have separate electorates. Gandhi began fast unto death on 20 th September, 1932 A. D. to protest against this decision. Finally, on 24 September, 1932 A. D. an agreement was made in Poona known as 'Poona Pact' in which joint electorate was accepted on the basis of two provisions. The two provisions were - Firstly, there were 148 seats reserved for depressed classes in the provincial legislature while only 71 seats were reserved according to communal award. In Central Legislature 18 percent of the seats allotted to the general electorate were reserved for depressed classes. So reason (R) explains assertion (A) correctly, and both statements are true. So, the option (a) is correct answer.
*Asked in:* U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2005

**Q12.** Dr. Ambedkar and Gandhiji had a Pact called :

- **A.** Calcutta Pact
- **B.** London Pact
- **C.** Poona Pact
- **D.** Lahore Pact

**Answer:** C — Poona Pact
**Explanation:** On 16 August, 1932 A. D., Ramsay Macdonald announced his Communal Award. The award authorised Indian Christians, Muslims, Europeans, Sikhs, Depressed Classes and others to have separate electorates. Gandhi began fast unto death on 20 th September, 1932 A. D. to protest against this decision. Finally, on 24 September, 1932 A. D. an agreement was made in Poona known as 'Poona Pact' in which joint electorate was accepted on the basis of two provisions. The two provisions were - Firstly, there were 148 seats reserved for depressed classes in the provincial legislature while only 71 seats were reserved according to communal award. In Central Legislature 18 percent of the seats allotted to the general electorate were reserved for depressed classes. So reason (R) explains assertion (A) correctly, and both statements are true. So, the option (a) is correct answer.
*Asked in:* Uttarakhand U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 2007; Uttarakhand P.C.S. (Mains) 2002

Birla, Rajagopalachari, Dr. Rajendra Prasad, Dr. Rao Bahadur Srinivasan, M. C. Rajah, C. V. Mehta, Bakhale and Kamath were other signatories. Many people signed on the document in Bombay. **Q16.** After Poona Pact of 1932, Harijan Sewak Sangh was established. Its President was:

**Answer:** B — Ghanshyam Das Birla

Ghanshyam Das Birla was the first President of this institution.
*Asked in:* U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2011; U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1994

**Q17.** Subsequent to which one of the following events, Gandhiji, who consistently opposed untouchability and appealed for its eradication from all spheres, decided to include the upliftment of 'Harijans' in his political and social programme?

- **A.** The Poona Pact
- **B.** The Gandhi-Irwin Agreement (Delhi Pact)
- **C.** Arrest of Congress leadership at the time of the Quit India Movement
- **D.** Promulgation of the Government of India Act, 1935

**Answer:** A — The Poona Pact
**Explanation:** After the Poona Pact (1932) and the end of the Yeravda fast that led to it, Gandhiji adopted the upliftment of Harijans as an organised, all-India political and social programme-the establishment of the Harijan Sevak Sangh (on September 30, 1932), the weekly 'Harijan', and the Harijan tours were direct expressions of this decision.

## 37. Congress Socialist Party (1934)

**Answer:** C — Patna
**Explanation:** Congress Socialist Party was established in May, 1934 A. D. in Patna during the meeting of Congress Committee. In October, 1934 A. D., the policies and systems of the Party were decided in Bombay.
*Asked in:* 44th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2000

**Answer:** B — 1934
**Explanation:** Congress Socialist Party was established in May, 1934 A. D. in Patna during the meeting of Congress Committee. In October, 1934 A. D., the policies and systems of the Party were decided in Bombay.
*Asked in:* 42nd B.P.S.C. (Pre) 1997

**Q3.** Consider the following statements regarding the Congress Socialist Party: 1. In January 1934, the Congress Socialist Party was formed. 2. Due to his sympathy for socialism, Jawaharlal Nehru formally joined this party. Which of the above statements is/are correct?

- **A.** Both 1 and 2
- **B.** Neither 1 nor 2
- **C.** Only 1
- **D.** Only 2

**Answer:** B — Neither 1 nor 2
**Explanation:** In 1934 AD, during the Congress Committee meeting in Patna, the formation of the All India Congress Socialist Party was formally recognized. In October 1934 AD, in Bombay, the party's policies and working principles were determined. In the same year, in Patna, Jayaprakash Narayan was one of the conveners of the All India Congress Socialist Party. Jayaprakash Narayan was elected as the party's General Secretary, and Narendra Dev was chosen as its President. Jawaharlal Nehru never formally joined this party.
*Asked in:* U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2024

**Q4.** With reference to Congress Socialist Party, consider the following statements: 1. It advocated the boycott of British goods and evasion of taxes. 2. It wanted to establish the dictatorship of the proletariat. 3. It advocated a separate electorate for minorities and oppressed classes. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

- **A.** 1 and 2 only
- **B.** 3 only
- **C.** 1, 2 and 3
- **D.** None of the above

**Answer:** D — None of the above
**Explanation:** The Congress Socialist Party was founded in 1934 A. D. as a socialist caucus within the INC. Its members rejected what they saw as the anti-rational mysticism of Gandhi as well as the sectarian attitude of the Communist Party of India towards the Congress party. Influenced by Fabianism as well as Marxism, the CSP advocated armed struggle as well as non-violent resistance. The CSP advocated decentralized socialism in which cooperation, trade unions, independent farmers and local authorities would hold a substantial share of economic power. As secularists, they hoped to transcend communal divisions through class solidarity. Hence, option (d) would be the correct answer.
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 2015

## 38. Provincial Election and Formation of Cabinet (1937)

**Q1.** Madras (159 seats out of total 215 seats) - Congress 2. Bihar (98 seats out of total 152 seats) - Congress 3. Central Provinces and Berar (70 out of 112) - Congress 4. United Provinces (134 seats out of 228) - Congress 5. Orissa (36 out of 60 seats) - Congress * Congress emerged as the single largest party in Bombay (86 seats out of 175), Assam and North-West Frontier Province. Only in Bengal, Punjab and Sindh did Congress not secure enough support from masses to form the government on its own. The cabinets formed by Congress after 1936-37 A.D. elections only lasted for 28 months. In July 1937 A.D., Congress formed cabinets in 6 provinces - Madras, Bombay, Central Province, Orissa, Bihar, and United Province and with the support of other parties Congress formed a coalition government in Assam (a coalition government was formed by Muhammad Saadulla in 1937, but later resigned and Congress government led by Gopinath Bordoloi took office in September 1938) and North-West Frontier Provinces. Based on 1937 results, Sir Sahibzada Abdul Qayyum Khan, formed a coalition government although Indian National Congress was the single largest party, the Congress formed the government there by moving no-confidence motion against Qayyum Khan. The inclusion of Indians into the Second World War without consultation led to the resignation of all Congress cabinets. On 22nd October, 1939 A.D. Congress cabinet of all provinces resigned as an act of protest. Congress coalition government in Assam under Gopinath Bordoloi was resigned from the government in November, 1939 and the NWFP government was also resigned in November, 1939. On the resignation of the Congress cabinets, Jinnah called Indian Muslims to celebrate 22nd December, 1939 A.D. as a Day of Deliverance. *Working Committee of Indian National Congress decided for abolition of feudal intermediaries/peasants proprietorship in 1937 A.D. as a result of which Congress governments in U.P. and Bihar passed tenancy bills. Congress secured 134 seats out of 228 seats in United Provinces and formed government on its own. *Govind Ballabh Pant was the Prime Minister (Premier) while Kailash Nath Katju was Law and Justice Minister and Revenue/Home/ Jail Ministry was given to RafiAhmed Kidwai. * In Congress- ruled states the reports related to Muslims grievances were in the following chronological order. - Pirpur Report - 1938 - Sharif Report - March, 1939 - Fazlul Haq Report (Muslims Sufferings Under Congress Rule Report) - December, 1939 1. In which of the following provinces did the Indian National Congress not obtain a full majority in provincial legislature elections held in 1937?

- **A.** Central Province
- **B.** Bihar
- **C.** Punjab
- **D.** Madras

**Answer:** C — Punjab
**Explanation:** Provincial assembly elections were held under the Indian Government Act, 1935 in which Congress won a full majority in 5 provinces - Madras, Bihar, Central Provinces and Berar, United Province and Orrisa. Congress made its ministries in 6 states: Madras, Central Province, Bihar, Bombay, Orissa and United Province in July, 1937 A. D. Only in Bengal, Punjab and Sindh Congress did not secure enough support.
*Asked in:* U.P P.C.S. (Pre) 1992

## 40. Indian Princely States

**Q1.** The purpose of the Butler Committee, 1927:

- **A.** Modernization of Indian Army
- **B.** Innovative modernization of Indian Agriculture.
- **C.** Implementation of censorship over National Newspapers.
- **D.** Improvement of relationships between Indian Provinces and the Crown.

**Answer:** D — Improvement of relationships between Indian Provinces and the Crown.
**Explanation:** The Indian States Committee appointed a committee under the Chairmanship of Sir Harcourt Butler, which was popularly known as 'The Butler Committee' to investigate and clarify the relationship between paramount power and the princes of Princely States in 1927 AD. The recommendations of committee were - The relationship of the paramount power of the state was not merely a contractual relationship but a living, growing relationship shaped by the circumstances and policy. British paramount preserved the princely State. The state should not be transferred without their agreement to a relationship with a new government in British India responsible to an Indian legislature.
*Asked in:* 46 B.P.C.S. (Pre) 2004

- **A.** in 1924
- **B.** in 1926
- **C.** in 1927
- **D.** in 1929

**Explanation:** All India State People's Conference was set up in December, 1927 A. D. More than 1500 political workers of different States participated in this Conference. **Q4.** Most of the integration of princely states in the Union of India had taken place in which year?

- **A.** 1948
- **B.** 1947
- **C.** 1950
- **D.** 1961

**Answer:** B — 1947
**Explanation:** Integration of most of the princely states happened in 1947 A. D. Most of the Princely States acceded in the Dominion of India in 1947 AD except Junagarh, Jammu & Kashmir and Hyderabad and these three States were compelled to join the Union of India till the end of 1948 A. D. Sardar Patel, who took charge of the state department in 1947 A. D., tackled the situation with great statesmanship. Patel appealed to the patriotic and nationalist sentiments of the Princes and requested the States to be handed over to the authority of External Affairs, Defence and Communications to the Indian Dominion. The integration of Princely states took proper shape in his leadership.

- **A.** Punjab

- **D.** Bihar

**Answer:** A — Punjab

*Asked in:* U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1997

**Q10.** During the freedom struggle, a parallel movement launched in the Indian States (in the States ruled by the Indian rulers such as Kashmir, Nizam's Hyderabad, Travancore etc.) was

- **A.** Swaraj Movement
- **B.** State People's Movement
- **C.** Praja Mandal Movement
- **D.** More than one of the above
- **E.** None of the above

**Answer:** C — Praja Mandal Movement
**Explanation:** In 1920s during freedom struggle various people's movements were launched in the princely states of British Raj. These movements were called State Peoples Conference or Praja Mandals. These movements were spearheaded by people living in princely states who were subject to the rule of local aristocrats rather than the British Raj. They campaigned against those feudatory rulers, and sometimes also the British administrators, in attempts to improve their civil rights.
*Asked in:* 68th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2022


## 41. Second World War

**Q1.** What was the policy of Indian National Congress during II World War? nd

- **A.** Cooperation of Britain in the case of assurance of Complete Independence.
- **B.** Active collaboration of British (Britain)
- **C.** Neutrality
- **D.** None of the above.

**Answer:** A — Cooperation of Britain in the case of assurance of Complete Independence.
**Explanation:** When World War II broke out in 1939 A. D., Britain made India belligerent without consulting Indian elected councils and also declared the Emergency. That action angered Indian officials and prompted the Congress Party to declare that India would not support the war until it had been granted complete independence.
*Asked in:* U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 1993

**Q2.** Statement (S) :Indian National Congress had collabo- rated/assisted British in II World War. nd Reason (R) : Because they were expecting to complete independence. Code :

- **A.** (S) and (R) are individually true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (S).
- **B.** Both (S) and (R) are false.
- **C.** (S) is true, but (R) is false.
- **D.** (R) is true, but (S) is false.

**Answer:** B — Both (S) and (R) are false.
**Explanation:** During the Second World War the proposal approved by Indian National Congress criticized Nazism, Fascism and the Nazi invasion of Poland. It was declared under the proposal that Indian could not take part in any such war which is being fought to protect the democratic liberty, while itself being deprived of liberty. Therefore, both the statement and the reason are incorrect.
*Asked in:* U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 1992

**Q3.** Assertion (A) :The Congress Ministries in all the provinces resigned in the year 1939. Reason (R) : The Congress did not accept the decision of the Viceroy to declare war against Germany in the context of the Second World War. Code:

- **A.** (A) and (R) are individually true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
- **B.** (A) and (R) are individually true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
- **C.** Both (A) and (R) are false.
- **D.** (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

**Answer:** A — (A) and (R) are individually true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
**Explanation:** On September 3, 1939 A. D. Lord Linlithgow declared India in the war against Germany. Congress cabinets had resigned from all the provinces for declaring war without the consent of the Congress Ministries. Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 2008

**Q4.** The Congress Ministries in all the provinces resigned in the year 1939, because :

- **A.** Congress was unable to make a cabinet in other four provinces.
- **B.** The rise of the left wing of Congress made impossible to work for the cabinet.
- **C.** There was too much communal turbulence in the provinces
- **D.** None of the above is true from the given statement (a), (b), (c).

**Answer:** D — None of the above is true from the given statement (a), (b), (c).
**Explanation:** After 28 months of tenure, the cabinets of Congress resigned in 1939 A. D. because British Government had declared India as a war-torn country without the consent of Indians. Thus, option (d) is true.
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 2012

**Q5.** When did the II World War end? nd

- **A.** 1937
- **B.** 1918

- **D.** 1945

**Answer:** D — 1945
**Explanation:** The Second World War commenced on September 1, 1939 A. D. with the invasion of Germany over Poland which ended after six years in 1945 A. D.

## 42. Demand for Pakistan

**Q1.** Who among the following had primarily used the word 'Pakistan' for separate State for Indian Muslims?

- **A.** Sir Mohammad Iqbal
- **B.** Sir Aga Khan
- **C.** M. A. Jinnah
- **D.** Chaudhary Rehmat Ali and his friends

**Answer:** D — Chaudhary Rehmat Ali and his friends
**Explanation:** The word PAKSTAN (later Pakistan) was primarily used by the student of Cambridge University Chaudhary Rahmat Ali in his letter entitled "Now or Never; Are we to Live or Perish for Ever?"
*Asked in:* R.A.S./R.T.S. (Pre) 1996

**Q2.** Who among the following first coined the word 'Pakistan'?

- **A.** Mohammad Ali Jinnah
- **B.** Choudhary Rehmat Ali
- **C.** Syed Ahmad Khan
- **D.** Mohammad Ashfaq Khan

**Answer:** B — Choudhary Rehmat Ali
**Explanation:** The term "Pakistan" or Pakstan (later became Pakistan) was first coined by Chaudhary Rahmat Ali, a Pakistani nationalist in a pamphlet published in 1933 A. D. The word was formed by combining the names of the regions that were to constitute the proposed nation: Punjab, Afghan Province (North-West Frontier Province), Kashmir, Sindh and Balochistan. The idea of Pakistan gained further momentum, leading to the creation of the independent state of Pakistan in 1947.
*Asked in:* M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2023

**Q3.** The idea of a separate Nation for Muslims was given by:

- **A.** Mohammad Ali Jinnah
- **B.** Sir Syed Ahmad Khan
- **C.** Sir Mohammad Iqbal
- **D.** Liaqat Ali Khan

**Answer:** C — Sir Mohammad Iqbal
**Explanation:** The poet and political philosopher Muhammad Iqbal is considered as the originator of the idea of a separate Muslim nation. Inspired by the spirit of Pan-Islam in All India Muslim League at Allahabad Session in 1930. Muhammad Iqbal said " I would like to see Punjab, the North-West Frontier Province, Sindh and Balochistan amalgamated into a single state. Self-government within the British Empire, or without the British Empire, formation of a consolidated North-West Indian Muslim state appears to me to be the final destiny of the Muslims, at least of North-West India.
*Asked in:* Uttarakhand P.C.S. (Mains) 2006; U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2003

**Q4.** Who among the following first put forward the proposal for a separate Muslim state in India?

- **A.** Agha Khan
- **B.** M.A. Jinnah
- **C.** Liaqat Ali Khan
- **D.** Mohammad Iqbal

**Answer:** D — Mohammad Iqbal
**Explanation:** During his landmark presidential address to the annual session of the All-India Muslim League at Allahabad in 1930, Iqbal declared Hindus and Muslims to be two separate nations in the light of the religious, social, cultural and historical context.
*Asked in:* U.P.R.O./A.R.O. (Mains) 2014

**Q5.** Who among following led the movement for the separate State Pakistan?

- **A.** Aga Khan
- **B.** Nawab Salim Ullah
- **C.** Liaqat Ali Khan
- **D.** Md. Ali Jinnah

**Answer:** D — Md. Ali Jinnah
**Explanation:** From March 22 to 24, 1940 A. D., the session of Muslim League was held at Lahore in the Presidentship of Mohammad Ali Jinnah. In this session, he demanded a separate Muslim autonomous state apart from India. Jinnah said in his speech that he would not accept anything other than a separate Muslim Nation.
*Asked in:* 38th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 1992

**Q6.** Who of the following called Mohammad Ali Jinnah as 'Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity' ?

- **A.** Sarojini Naidu
- **B.** Annie Besant
- **C.** Rajkumari Amrit Kaur
- **D.** Aruna Asaf Ali

**Answer:** A — Sarojini Naidu
**Explanation:** In 1919 A. D. when Jinnah was giving testimony in front of Parliament Select Committee, then he was asked: "Are you saying this as a virtue of the Indian Nationalist"? In reply, he firmly said, "yes, I am saying this as a virtue of Indian Nationalist." After that, Major Oksbergi asked, "means you want to finish the discrimination between Muslim and Hindu at the earliest?" In answer, Jinnah said- 'yes, I will be the happiest person when that day comes.' For these Nationalist views and to compromising Muslim League and Congress Sarojini Naidu hailed him "Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity."
*Asked in:* U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2004; U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2000

**Q7.** The remark 'Nehru is a patriot, while Jinnah is a politician' was made by:

- **A.** M.K Gandhi
- **B.** Maulana Azad
- **C.** Sir Mohammad Iqbal
- **D.** Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan

**Answer:** C — Sir Mohammad Iqbal
**Explanation:** The first Prime Minister of India Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru in page 352 of his book "Discovery of India" mentioned that Muhammad Iqbal during a meeting with him remarked, "you (Nehru) are a patriot, while Jinnah is a politician".
*Asked in:* U.P.P.S.C. (GIC) 2010; U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1991

**Q8.** Which of the following statements is not true about Muhammad Ali Jinnah?

- **A.** He was the supporter of two-nation theory.
- **B.** He presided the Lahore session of Muslim League in 1940.
- **C.** He had not participated in the Non-Cooperation Movement.
- **D.** He always had dairy.

**Answer:** D — He always had dairy.
**Explanation:** Jinnah was a supporter of two-nation theory. While chairing the Lahore Session of Muslim League between 22-24 March 1940 A. D. he demanded a separate Muslim nation apart from India. Sir Sikandar Hayat Khan, Fazlul-Haq, and Khaliquzzaman played an important role in preparing an outline for the proposal of Pakistan. Mohammad Ali Jinnah was not a supporter of Non-Cooperation Movement, so he did not participate in this movement.
*Asked in:* U.P. U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 2008

**Q9.** A separate homeland for Muslims found for the first time a definite expression :

- **A.** In the Presidential Speech of Iqbal at the Allahabad Session of Muslim League (1930).
- **B.** In the Cambridge Pamphlet.
- **C.** In the Lahore Session of Muslim League in 1940.
- **D.** None of the above.

**Answer:** A — In the Presidential Speech of Iqbal at the Allahabad Session of Muslim League (1930).

C. Majumdar- The history and culture of the Indian people: struggle for freedom, page No.- 613). The limited individual Satyagrah had two aims - to show the displeasure of people of India with British India's participation in war and to give another chance to British government to accept demands of Indian people. Gandhiji and Congress, did not want to disrupt war efforts of British by starting mass movement due to their anti-Nazi stand.

## 45. Quit India Movement

**Q1.** ) Government officials should announce their support and devotion to Congress. 2) Soldiers should refuse to fire on their countrymen. 3) Students should quit studies only if they stood firmly on this decision until independence. 4) Kings should accept the sovereignty of their people and declare their province as a part of the Indian nation. Masses should accept the leadership of the king only if he sees his future in the future of Masses. *In his speech Gandhiji said :- "I am not going to be satisfied with anything short than complete freedom". It may be possible that Salt Tax and drink evil, etc. may be abolished or stopped by the English Government but my words will demand 'Nothing less than complete Freedom'. Today I give you a mantra "Do or Die". This mantra means that either we will free our country or will die fighting for Independence. *On 8th August, 1942 A.D., Jawahar Lal Nehru presented the 'Quit India resolution' to All India Congress Committee. This proposal was supported by Sardar Vallabh Bhai Patel. The draft of this proposal was prepared by Mahatma Gandhi himself with the help of Jawahar Lal. *Hindu Mahasabha, Communist Party of India, Unionist Party (Punjab) and Muslim League were not in favour of this movement. On 9th August, 1942 A.D., Quit India Movement was launched. In the early hours of the Movement, Gandhiji and other important leaders of Congress were arrested under Operation Zero Hour. *Gandhiji, Sarojini Naidu and other leaders were arrested and taken to Aga Khan Palace. *Members of Congress working Committee (Jawaharlal Nehru, Abul Kalam Azad, Govind Ballabh Pant, Dr. Prafful Chandra Ghosh, Dr. Pattabhi Sitaramayya, Dr. Syed Mahmud, Acharya Kriplani) were arrested and taken to Ahmednagar Fort. *Dr. Rajendra Prasad, member of Congress Working Committee couldn't come to Bombay, he was arrested and kept at Patna (Bankipur) Jail. Shivkumar and Ram-nandan Mishra (he was first arrested in Cuttack but later he was transferred to Hzaribagh). were arrested in Hazaribagh. *Movement of 1942 showed maximum impact in Bombay, Bengal, Bihar, Orissa, United Province of Agra and Oudh and Madras but the participation of the whole country was necessary for this movement to succeed. *Lord Wavell was the commander in chief of India during Quit India Movement (1942 A.D.). He served as Viceroy from the year 1943 A.D. to 1947 A.D. *Winston Churchill was the Prime Minister of England during Quit India Movement. *Abul Kalam Azad was the President of Congress when the resolution of Quit India Movement was passed. He was elected President in Ramgarh Session of Congress in 1940 A.D. and after that for five years (1941-45 A.D.) no session of Congress was held and Abul Kalam Azad continued to be the President of Congress for these years. He was the President of Congress for the maximum years before independence, also the political scenario of India was very fragile during his tenure. *During Quit India Movement, a secret radio station of Congress was broadcasted from different parts of Bombay Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia played a significant role in the Quit India Movement. He directed the movement while remaining underground. He also established an undergraound radio station. *Usha Mehta was an important member of the group of Congress that broadcasted radio being underground. *Louis Fischer, an American journalist, was with Gandhiji just before Quit India Movement as he came to India in May 1942 and spent one week with Gandhiji at Sevagram Ashram, Wardha. (He was biographer of Gandhiji). *Louis Fischer, with American intellectuals Pearl Buck, Edgar Snow, Fredrick L. Schuman and Norman Thomas demanded India's Independence. *Riots emerging out of Quit India Movement were widespread in Bihar and United Provinces It emerged as a revolt. Eastern United Provinces (including Azamgarh, Ballia, Gorakhpur) and Gaya, Champaran, Saran, Purnia, Shahabad, Muzaffarpur, and Bhagalpur areas of Bihar were self instilled centres of mass revolt. *August Movement of 1942 A.D. became widespread among the farmers. Some groups of farmers performed agricultural activities in the day and took part in rioting activities at night. Their fierceness and strength demonstrated the glimpses of the revolt of 1857, that is why Viceroy Linlithgow in a telegram to British Prime Minister Winston Churchill termed this movement as by far the most serious rebellion after the Revolt of 1857. *During the Quit India Movement, Jayaprakash Narayan fled from Hazaribagh jail and became active in the underground activities. Yogendra Shukla too fled with J.P. Narayan on 9th November, 1942 A.D. but was later arrested in Muzaffarpur and sent to Patna. *On the speech given by Gandhiji during Quit India Movement (1942 A.D.), Pattabhi Sitaramayya said, "In reality that day Gandhiji was speaking after being motivated with the power of Avatar and Paigambar. *Rashtriya Swayam Sevak Sangh didn't participate in Quit India Movement. It didn't participate in any movement between 1940 A.D. and 1947 A.D. till foreign rule ended. *Aruna Asaf Ali was a famous freedom fighter. She will always be remembered for hoisting the tricolour Flag at Gowalia Tank ground (Bombay) during Quit India Movement. *Aruna Asaf Ali, Usha Mehta, J.P. Narayan, Ram Manohar Lohia, etc being underground provided alternate leadership to the Quit India Movement when all other prominent leaders were arrested. *Establishment of Parallel Government at several places was an important feature of Quit India Movement. These were:- 1. Ballia - August 1942 A.D. - Chittu Pandey led the Government. 2. Tamluk (Midnapore) Bengal - From December 1942 to August 1944 AD the Tamralipta Jatiya Sarkar in Tamluk started the relief programmes for the persons affected by storms. 3. Satara (Maharashtra) - A Parallel Government named Prati Sarkar was formed in August-1943 A.D. It was the longest-serving Parallel Government till May 1946 A.D. Its main leaders were - Y.B. Chavan and Nana Patil. There was a Parallel Government in Talchar, Orissa too for some time. *Gandhiji was released on 6th May, 1944 A.D. on account of bad health conditions. On Gandhiji's release, Winston Churchill remarked, "When we are winning around the globe how can we be defeated by this old man who is our enemy for a long time." 1. On 6th July, 1942, at the Working Committee of the Congress, Mahatma Gandhi discussed for the first time his 'Quit India Policy'. The President of the Committee was :

- **A.** Rajagopalachari
- **B.** Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
- **C.** Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru
- **D.** Dr. Annie Besant

**Answer:** B — Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
**Explanation:** In July, 1942 A. D., the meeting of Congress Working Committee was held at Wardha in which Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabh Bhai Patel, Pattabhi Sitaramaiyya, Achyut Patwardhan, Dr. Anugraha Narayan Sinha, Aruna Asaf Ali, Mahatma Gandhi etc. had taken part and passed a resolution named 'Quit India Movement', was chaired by the then Congress President Maulana Abul Kalam Azad.

**Q4.** Quit India movement began on:

- **A.** 9th August, 1942
- **B.** 10th August, 1942
- **C.** 15th August, 1942
- **D.** 16th August, 1942

**Answer:** A — 9th August, 1942
**Explanation:** The historic session of the All India Congress Committee began on the 7th August, 1942 A. D. and concluded on 8th August, 1942 A. D. at Gowalia Tank Maidan (now August Kranti Ground), Bombay. Quit India movement began on 9th August, 1942 A. D. The Committee asserted India's right to freedom and decided to start a mass struggle with nonviolent means on the widest possible scale. Addressing the conference, Gandhiji gave the call "Do or Die," either to get India free or to die in this attempt. But before the Movement could be launched Gandhiji and all other leaders of the Congress were imprisoned under Operation Zero Hour. Gandhiji and Sarojini Naidu were kept in Aga Khan Palace at Poona (now Pune). The Movement of 1942 A. D. mostly affected the State of Bombay, Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, United Province (U. P.) and Madras. Though the whole country participated in this Movement.

**Q5.** Quit India Movement was started on __________.

- **A.** 7th August, 1942
- **B.** 9th August, 1942
- **C.** 10th August, 1942
- **D.** 6th August, 1942

**Answer:** B — 9th August, 1942
**Explanation:** The historic session of the All India Congress Committee began on the 7th August, 1942 A. D. and concluded on 8th August, 1942 A. D. at Gowalia Tank Maidan (now August Kranti Ground), Bombay. Quit India movement began on 9th August, 1942 A. D. The Committee asserted India's right to freedom and decided to start a mass struggle with nonviolent means on the widest possible scale. Addressing the conference, Gandhiji gave the call "Do or Die," either to get India free or to die in this attempt. But before the Movement could be launched Gandhiji and all other leaders of the Congress were imprisoned under Operation Zero Hour. Gandhiji and Sarojini Naidu were kept in Aga Khan Palace at Poona (now Pune). The Movement of 1942 A. D. mostly affected the State of Bombay, Bengal, Bihar, Odisha, United Province (U. P.) and Madras. Though the whole country participated in this Movement.
*Asked in:* M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2022

**Q14.** Consider the following statements- On the eve of launch of Quit India Movement, Mahatma Gandhi: 1. Asked Government servants to resign. 2. Asked the soldiers to leave their posts. 3. - **B.** 2 and 3
- **C.** 3 only
- **D.** 1, 2 and 3

Thus, only 3rd statement is correct.

**Q24.** Which one of the following observations is not true about the Quit India Movement of 1942?

- **A.** It was a non-violent Movement.
- **B.** It was led by Mahatma Gandhi.
- **C.** It was a spontaneous Movements.
- **D.** It did not attract the labour class in general.

**Answer:** not given in source
**Explanation:** Quit India Movement of 1942 A. D. was not so non-violent. According to official assessments, in first week 250 railway stations were either damaged or destroyed, and more than 500 post offi ces and 150 police stations were attacked. Heavy violence was used for the suppression of the movement from the ruling party. Mahatma Gandhi himself in 1942 A. D. refused to condemn the violence. He said it was an answer to the huge violence of the rulers. The arrest of the main leaders (including Gandhiji) before even start of movement had made the movement more aggressive and spontaneous. The movement did not attract the labour class in general (due to reasons like monetary constraints, fear of repression, effect of trade unions etc.) in comparison to other sections of society like students, farmers etc. Thus, options (a) and (b) are individually not correct.
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 2011

**Q35.** 'Quit India Movement' was reaction of- (1) The disappointment of Indians against Cripps Mission. (2) The threat of Japanese attack on India. (3) To provoke countrymen to adopt violent means by Gandhiji's articles. (4) Due to passing the proposal of August, 1942 by AICC. Choose the answer using the given options-

- **A.** 1 and 2
- **B.** 1,2 and 4
- **C.** 2,3. and 4
- **D.** All of the above

**Answer:** B — 1,2 and 4
**Explanation:** After the failure of Cripps Mission in March, 1942 A. D., it seemed clear that the British Government wanted to continue the partnership with India in Second World War without their consent but was not ready for any sacred agreement. Gandhiji declared in his 'Do or Die' speech ' that "I do not want to make the instrument either of Russia's defeat or of China's." But it seemed by spring 1942 A. D. that the struggle was inevitable. Thus, Congress passed Quit India Resolution in August, 1942 A. D. Gandhiji had never provoked to adoption of violent means in his articles. Thus, statement 3 is not correct while the other statements are correct about 'Quit India Movement.'

**Q47.** Assertion (A) : Lord Linlithgow described the August Movement of 1942 as the most serious rebellion since Sepoy Mutiny. Reason (R) : There was a massive upsurge of the peasantry in certain areas.

- **A.** Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
- **B.** Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not a correct explanation of A.
- **C.** (A) is true, but (R) is false.
- **D.** (A) is false, but (R) is true.

**Answer:** A — Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
**Explanation:** The involvement of peasants in Quit India Movement made the struggle more violent. This forced Linlithgow to describe the Quit India Movement launched on 9th August, 1942 A. D. as the most serious rebellion since Sepoy Mutiny of 1857. Thus, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 1999

**Q48.** Dr. Rajendra Prasad was arrested on 9th August, 1942 and was sent to :

Dr. Rajendra Prasad, a member of Congress Working Committee, was not in Bombay thus, he was arrested in Patna under Bharat Security Rules and sent to Patna (Bankipur) jail.

**Q53.** With the news of Gandhi and other Congress leaders arrest in 1942, a riot in Bihar took place, leading to a total breakdown in the rail services. The most affected area was :

- **A.** Munger
- **B.** Gaya
- **C.** Patna
- **D.** Shahabad

**Answer:** A — Munger
**Explanation:** On August 9, 1942 Gandhiji and other main leaders of Congress were arrested. Police launched a suppression cycle to crack down on the Movement. Outraged by the suppression of the police, the public attacked at several places. Police stations, Railway stations and post offi ces were on their targets. Rail lines were uprooted at several places. As a result, rail services were disrupted completely. Medinipur district of Bengal, Baliya district of Uttar Pradesh and Munger district of Bihar were the centers of public anger. The incident of uprooting railway tracks had mostly happened in Bihar. Munger was the most affected district which remained cut off from the outside world for 2 weeks.

**Q59.** Who among the following women freedom fighters was not associated with 'Quit India Movement'?

- **A.** Matangini Hazra
- **B.** Kanak Lata Barua
- **C.** Aruna Asaf Ali
- **D.** Shanti Ghosh

**Answer:** D — Shanti Ghosh
**Explanation:** Matangini Hazra was 73 years old when she fell to British bullets, leading a protest March in 1942 A. D. in Tamluk, Bengal during the Quit India Movement. Kanaklata Barua was an Indian freedom fighter and AISF leader. She joined the Mrityu Bahini ('Death Army'), a death squad comprising group of youth from the Gohpur sub-division of Assam in line with Gandhiji's 'Do or Die' call during 'Quit India Movement'. She was shot dead in September 1942 while bearing the National flag at age of about 17 in Borangabari, Gohpur, Assam. Aruna Asaf Ali was an Indian educator, political activist and publisher. An active participant in the Indian Independence movement, she is widely remembered for hoisting the Indian National Flag at the Gowalia Tank maidan (now August Kranti Ground), Bombay (Mumbai) during Quit India Movement in 1942 A. D. Shanti Ghosh was an active member of the revolutionary group, Yugantar. On 14th December, 1931 A. D. Shanti Ghosh along with Suniti entered the bungalow of a District Magistrate with a pistol and shot him dead at point-blank range. Hence, option (d) is correct answer.

**Q60.** Assertion(A) : Quit India Movement succeeded in awakening and encouraging people. Reason (R) : People have assimilated the slogan of 'Do or Die.' In above context, which of the following is correct?

**Answer:** A — (A) and (R) are individually true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Soon after the arrest of Gandhi, rioting broke out immediately throughout the country and many violent demonstrations took place. Quit India became the most powerful movement in the freedom struggle. Thousands of freedom fighters were arrested. He called on all Congressmen and Indians to maintain discipline via non-violence and Do or Die (Karo Ya Maro) to achieve ultimate freedom. Thus, Quit India Movement succeeded in awakening and encouraging people, assimilating the slogan of 'Do or Die.'

**Q72.** Assertion (A) :The Quit India Movement marked the culmination of Indian National Movement. Reason (R) : After the Quit India Movement there was a need of time to find a suitable mechanism for transfer of power. Select the correct answer from the code given below: Code :

- **A.** (A) and (R) are individually true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
- **B.** (A) and (R) are individually true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
- **C.** (A) is true, but (R) is false.
- **D.** (A) is false, but (R) is true.

**Answer:** A — (A) and (R) are individually true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
**Explanation:** The Quit India Movement, though short-lived and badly crushed gave the signals that the British rule was not wanted in India. There was nothing to stop Indians from attaining their freedom. The signs of the firm determination of the people to free India from the British hastened the British decision to quit.
*Asked in:* U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2005

**Q73.** After Quit India Movement, C. Rajagopalachari issued a pamphlet entitled "The Way Out." Which one of the following was a proposal in this pamphlet?

- **A.** The establishment of a "War Advisory Council" composed of representatives of British India and the Indian States
- **B.** Reconstitution of the Central Executive Council in such a way that all its members, except the Governor- General and the Commander-in-Chief, should be Indian leaders
- **C.** Fresh elections to the Central and Provincial Legislatures to be held at the end of 1945 and the Constitution-making body to be convened as soon as possible
- **D.** A solution to the Constitutional deadlock

**Answer:** D — A solution to the Constitutional deadlock
**Explanation:** C. Rajagopalachari's formula was a proposal formulated by Chakravarthi Rajagopalachari to solve the political deadlock between INC and All India Muslim League regarding Independence of India from the British. Rajagopalachari devised a proposal in 1944 A. D. called 'The way out' for Congress to offer the league the Muslim Pakistan based on plebiscite (the direct vote of all the members of an electorate on an important public question such as a change in the Constitution). The formula was opposed even by Congress. Jinnah also rejected the proposal and the talks failed.
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 2010

**Q74.** 'Operation Rubicon' was the code word proposed to be adopted by British Government in India with reference to which of the following?

- **A.** Gandhi's fast unto death in Jail
- **B.** Activities of Jai Prakash Narayan
- **C.** Gandhi's participation in Round Table Conference
- **D.** None of the above

**Answer:** A — Gandhi's fast unto death in Jail
**Explanation:** During Quit India movement while imprisoned in the Aga Khan Palace, Mahatma Gandhi's health was rapidly declining due to his fast unto death. 'Operation Rubicon' was secret code word to be adopted by the British Government in India, if Gandhiji died..
*Asked in:* R.O./A.R.O. (Pre) 2017


## 46. Subhash Chandra Bose and Azad Hind Fauj

**Q1.** Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose was born in the city of :

- **A.** Cuttack
- **B.** Calcutta
- **C.** Midnapore
- **D.** Murshidabad

**Answer:** A — Cuttack
**Explanation:** Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose was born on 23 January, 1897 A. D. in Cuttack of Odisha division of Bengal province. He graduated from Scottish Church College (Affiliated to Calcutta University) in 1919 A. D. and was selected in I. C.S. (Indian Civil Services) in 1920 A. D. He became the President of Congress in 1938 A. D. and 1939 A. D. He founded Forward Bloc in 1939 A. D. and fled away to Germany in 1941 A. D. In 1943 A. D., he gained control of Azad Hind Fauz. He was given title of Netaji here.
*Asked in:* U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2006

- **A.** Indian Freedom Party
- **B.** Azad Hind Fauj

**Answer:** D — Forward Bloc
**Explanation:** Subhas Chandra Bose resigned from the Presidentship of Congress after Tripuri Crisis and Founded 'Forward Bloc in 1939.

**Q7.** Which of the following statements about Subhas Chandra Bose are correct? 1. He was elected President of the Indian National Congress at Tripuri session of 1938 A.D. 2. He escaped from home internment in January 1941 A.D. 3. On October 21 1943 A.D. he constituted the Provincial Government of India in Singapore.

- **A.** Only 1 and 2
- **B.** Only 2 and 3
- **C.** Only 1 and 3
- **D.** 1, 2 and 3

**Answer:** B — Only 2 and 3
**Explanation:** In 1938, the 51st annual session of the Congress was held at Haripura (Gujarat), not at Tripuri. Subhas Chandra Bose presided over the Haripura session. The 52nd annual session of the Congress was held at Tripuri (Madhya Pradesh) in 1939 under the presidentship of Subhas Chandra Bose; later, he resigned from the post. Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose escaped at night from house arrest in January 1941 by disguising himself and successfully carried out his plan to leave Calcutta. He formed the Provisional Government of India at Singapore on 21 October 1943. Therefore, the correct answer is option (b). In the English version of this question, "Provincial" was mistakenly printed in place of "Provisional"; therefore, the Bihar Public Service Commission removed this question from evaluation.
*Asked in:* 71st B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2025

**Q8.** I.N.A. was brainchild of : 1. Gyani Pritam Singh 2. Mohan Singh 3. Subhash Chandra Bose 4. Major Iwaichi Fujiwara Select correct answer by using codes given below:

- **A.** 1 and 2
- **B.** 2 and 3
- **C.** 1 and 3
- **D.** 1 and 4

**Answer:** D — 1 and 4
**Explanation:** The Indian National Army (INA) was the brainchild of Giani Pritam Singh Dhillon along with Mohan Singh Major Fujiwara and on 15 July, 1942 The Indian National Army was formed under the leadership of Mohan Singh. Giani Pritam Singh became actively involved in the Indian Independence Movement and Gadar Party. He met with Iwaichi Fujiwara, who had even before the declaration of war by Japan, reached an agreement of collaboration with the Japanese at Bangkok in December, 1941. It was Giani Pritam Singh's idea working with Iwaichi Fujiwara who released Indian soldiers who were asked to join an Indian National Army to fight for Indian independence. These plans were started long before the war broke out, among a group of revolutionaries based in Bangkok. Thus, Capt. Mohan Singh was not the founder of INA, but was only the first operational Commander of the INA. He accepted the position at the insistence of Giani Ji and Iwaichi Fujiwara. The brains behind INA were Iwaichi Fujiwara and Giani Pritam Singh Dhillon.
*Asked in:* U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2001

**Q9.** The result of whose brain is I.N.A. and who founded it?

- **A.** Subhash Chandra Bose
- **B.** Mohan Singh
- **C.** Chandra Shekhar Azad
- **D.** Bhagat Singh

**Answer:** B — Mohan Singh
**Explanation:** The Indian National Army (INA) was the brainchild of Giani Pritam Singh Dhillon along with Mohan Singh Major Fujiwara and on 15 July, 1942 The Indian National Army was formed under the leadership of Mohan Singh. Giani Pritam Singh became actively involved in the Indian Independence Movement and Gadar Party. He met with Iwaichi Fujiwara, who had even before the declaration of war by Japan, reached an agreement of collaboration with the Japanese at Bangkok in December, 1941. It was Giani Pritam Singh's idea working with Iwaichi Fujiwara who released Indian soldiers who were asked to join an Indian National Army to fight for Indian independence. These plans were started long before the war broke out, among a group of revolutionaries based in Bangkok. Thus, Capt. Mohan Singh was not the founder of INA, but was only the first operational Commander of the INA. He accepted the position at the insistence of Giani Ji and Iwaichi Fujiwara. The brains behind INA were Iwaichi Fujiwara and Giani Pritam Singh Dhillon.
*Asked in:* 39th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 1994

**Q11.** In which year was the Indian National Army founded?

- **A.** 1940
- **B.** 1941
- **C.** 1942
- **D.** 1943

**Answer:** C — 1942
**Explanation:** In February, 1942 The Indian National Army was formed under the leadership of Mohan Singh. He was the first commander of Azad Hind Fauz. The unit was dissolved in December, 1942 after apprehensions of Japanese motives with regard to the INA led to disagreements and distrust between Mohan Singh and INA leadership on the one hand and the League's leadership, most notably Rash Behari Bose on the other. A large number of the INA's initial volunteers however, later went on to join the INA in its second incarnation under Subhash Chandra Bose. Bose arrived in Singapore on 2 July 1943 and on 4th July, 1943, Rash Behari Bose gave the command of I. N.A. to Subhash Chandra Bose. In October, 1943 Bose formally announced the establishment of the Provisional Government of Free India and took charge of INA.

**Q34.** Which soldier of Azad Hind Fauj was sentenced to seven years imprisonment?

- **A.** Aruna Asaf Ali
- **B.** Shahnawaz
- **C.** Rashid Ali
- **D.** Ras Behari Bose

**Answer:** C — Rashid Ali
**Explanation:** In the year 1945, Rashid Ali, Colonel Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon, Colonel Prem Kumar Sahgal and General Shahnawaz Khan were arrested by the British Forces and sent to Red Fort at Delhi for court-martial. After the end of the war, Colonel Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon, Colonel Prem Kumar Sahgal and General Shahnawaz Khan were put on trial in Delhi for waging war against the British Empire. Rashid Ali was sentenced to seven-years imprisonment while other prisoners faced the transportation for life punishment. The defence of the INA prisoners was taken up by the Congress and Bhulabhai Desai, Tej Bahadur Sapru, K. N. Katju, Jawahar Lal Nehru and Asaf Ali appeared in court at the historic Red Fort trials. The growing Nationalist sentiments developed into violent confrontations with authority and pressure from the political parties from India; Commanderin-Chief Field Marshal Sir Claude Auchinleck was forced to let the defendants go free.
*Asked in:* U.P.P.C.S. (Spl) (Pre) 2008

They were charged with waging war against the King as well as murder and attempt to Murder. The Congress formed a Defence Committee which included Bhulabhai Desai, Tej Bahadur Sapru, K. N. Katju, J. L. Nehru and Asaf Ali. Bhulabhai was the leading counsel for the defence. Muslim League also joined in this all India agitation.

## 47. Cabinet Mission Plan (1946)

**Q1.** Cabinet Mission was presided over by :

- **A.** Lord Attlee
- **B.** Stafford Cripps
- **C.** Clement Attlee
- **D.** Sir P. Lawrence

**Answer:** D — Sir P. Lawrence
**Explanation:** End of World War II saw the Labour Party under Mr. Attlee win elections in England (U. K.). Mr. Attlee was sympathetic towards India's demand for freedom. The British Prime Minister Clement Attlee announced on February 19, 1946 A. D. the dispatch of the Mission for Constitutional reforms. The Cabinet Mission arrived in Delhi on 24 March, 1946 A. D. The Cabinet Mission to India consisted of the Secretary of State for India Lord Pethick Lawrence, Sir Stafford Cripps (President of the Board of Trade) and A. V. Alexander (First Lord of the Admiralty).
*Asked in:* 45th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2001

**Q2.** The 'Cabinet-Mission' of 1946 was led by:

- **A.** Sir Pethick-Lawrence
- **B.** Lord Linlithgow
- **C.** Lord Wavell
- **D.** Sir John Simon

**Answer:** A — Sir Pethick-Lawrence
**Explanation:** End of World War II saw the Labour Party under Mr. Attlee win elections in England (U. K.). Mr. Attlee was sympathetic towards India's demand for freedom. The British Prime Minister Clement Attlee announced on February 19, 1946 A. D. the dispatch of the Mission for Constitutional reforms. The Cabinet Mission arrived in Delhi on 24 March, 1946 A. D. The Cabinet Mission to India consisted of the Secretary of State for India Lord Pethick Lawrence, Sir Stafford Cripps (President of the Board of Trade) and A. V. Alexander (First Lord of the Admiralty).
*Asked in:* U.P.P.C.S. (Re. Exam) (Pre) 2015

**Q3.** Who was not a member of the Cabinet Mission?

- **A.** Pethick-Lawrence
- **B.** Wavell
- **C.** Stafford Cripps
- **D.** A.V. Alexander
- **E.** None of the above/More than one of the above

**Answer:** B — Wavell
**Explanation:** End of World War II saw the Labour Party under Mr. Attlee win elections in England (U. K.). Mr. Attlee was sympathetic towards India's demand for freedom. The British Prime Minister Clement Attlee announced on February 19, 1946 A. D. the dispatch of the Mission for Constitutional reforms. The Cabinet Mission arrived in Delhi on 24 March, 1946 A. D. The Cabinet Mission to India consisted of the Secretary of State for India Lord Pethick Lawrence, Sir Stafford Cripps (President of the Board of Trade) and A. V. **Q12.** 'It made its proposals in May. It still wanted a united India. There was to be the Federal Union composed of British provinces'. The above quotation is related to:

**Q15.** With reference to the Cabinet Mission, which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. It recommended a federal Government. 2. It enlarged the powers of the Indian courts. 3. It provided for more Indians in the ICS. Select the correct answer using the code given below:

- **A.** 1 only
- **B.** 2 and 3
- **C.** 1 and 3
- **D.** None

**Answer:** A — 1 only
**Explanation:** The Cabinet Mission reached Delhi on 24 March, 1946 AD. The Cabinet Mission announced its recommendations on 16th May, 1946 AD. The main provision of the recommendations were: (1) The whole of India, including the Princely States should form a Federation. (2)The Central Government should be in charge of foreign affairs, defence and communication. (3) The provinces and the states should enjoy all the powers. The British Indian Provinces and territories were to be divided into three groups; Group A: Madras, Central Provinces and Berar, United Province, Bihar, Bombay and Orissa. Group B: Punjab, North-West Frontier Province and Sindh. Group C: Bengal and Assam. Apart from this, the Provinces of Chief Commissioners, Delhi, Ajmer-Marwar and Coorg will be included in category (A) and Baluchistan will be included in category (B). The Constituent Assembly was to be elected to frame a Constitution for the Indian Union. The province should have the right to leave the Union in future if it so likes after elections under its new Constitution. There should be an interim National Government with leaders of the Indian parties to take charge of the administration.
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 2015

The main provision of the recommendations were: (1) The whole of India, including the Princely States should form a Federation. (2)The Central Government should be in charge of foreign affairs, defence and communication. (3) The provinces and the states should enjoy all the powers. The British Indian Provinces and territories were to be divided into three groups; Group A: Madras, Central Provinces and Berar, United Province, Bihar, Bombay and Orissa. Group B: Punjab, North-West Frontier Province and Sindh. Group C: Bengal and Assam. Apart from this, the Provinces of Chief Commissioners, Delhi, Ajmer-Marwar and Coorg will be included in category (A) and Baluchistan will be included in category (B). The Constituent Assembly was to be elected to frame a Constitution for the Indian Union. The province should have the right to leave the Union in future if it so likes after elections under its new Constitution. There should be an interim National Government with leaders of the Indian parties to take charge of the administration.

**Q17.** The Cabinet Mission was sent to India for which of the following? 1. To establish a national government 2. To work out a constitutional arrangement for the transfer of power 3. To work out the details of Jinnah demand for Pakistan

- **A.** 3 only
- **B.** 1 only

- **E.** None of the above

**Q18.** Given below are two statements, one is labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R). Assertion (A) : In 1946, the Muslim League withdrew its acceptance of the Cabinet Mission Plan. Reason (R) : The Muslim League joined the interim government formed in 1946. Select the correct answer from the codes given below.

- **A.** Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
- **B.** Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
- **C.** (A) is true, but (R) is false.
- **D.** (A) is false, but (R) is true.

**Answer:** B — Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
**Explanation:** The Cabinet Mission of 1946 AD came to India to discuss the transfer of power from the British Government to the Indian Leadership, with the aim of preserving India's unity and granting it independence formulated at the initiative of Clement Attlee, the Prime Minister of United Kingdom, the mission included Lord Pethick-Lawrence, the secretary of state for India, Sir Stafford Cripps, President of the Board of Trade and A. V. Alexander, the first Lord of the Admiralty. Lord Wavell, the Viceroy of India, did not participate in every step but was present. The Mission arrived on March 24, 1946 AD. According to the Mission, the representation of the Provincial Legislatures were to be broken up into 3 sections (a) Section A: Madras, United Provinces, Central Province and Berar, Bombay, Bihar & Orissa. (b) Section B: Punjab, Sindh, NWFP (c) Section C: Assam and Bengal. Apart from this, the Provinces of Chief Commissioners, Delhi, Ajmer-Marvar and Coorg will be included in category (A) and Baluchistan will be included in category (B). The Congress accepted the proposals related to the constituent assembly. But since, the Muslim league had been given disproportionate representation; it rejected the idea of the interim government. The Muslim League first approved the Plan. But when congress, declared that it could change the scheme through majority in the Constituent Assembly they rejected the plan. Muslim League on repeated request by Lord Wavell joined the Interim Government on 13 October, 1946 AD.
*Asked in:* U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2018

## 48. Constituent Assembly (1946)

**Q1.** Which one of the following first mooted the idea of a Constituent Assembly to frame a Constitution for India?

- **A.** Swaraj Party in 1935
- **B.** Congress Party in 1936
- **C.** Muslims League in 1942
- **D.** All Parties Conference in 1946

**Answer:** B — Congress Party in 1936
**Explanation:** The idea of the Constitution of India was seen in 'Swaraj Bill' of 1895 for the first time but officially it was stated in the Faizpur Congress Session in 1936 AD. In this session, the constituent Assembly was vastly explained. It is notable that if option (a) would be Swaraj Party, 1934 then it would be the correct answer. The Swaraj Party demanded the development of Constituent Assembly in Ranchi (1934 AD).
*Asked in:* U.P.U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 2001

**Q2.** The Constituent Assembly that framed India's constitution was set up -

- **A.** Under the Indian Independence Act
- **B.** Under the Government of India Act, 1935
- **C.** By the Queen's Proclamation
- **D.** Under the Cabinet Mission Plan

**Answer:** D — Under the Cabinet Mission Plan
**Explanation:** Constituent Assembly was founded under Cabinet Mission. The President of Cabinet Mission declared that the main purpose of this mission was to make a Constitution Committee for Constitutional reforms in India. According to the Proposals of the Cabinet Mission, the assembly of the constituent assembly will be constituted by the representatives of the legislative assembly of provinces, the chief commissioners and the representatives of the princely states.
*Asked in:* U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2008; U.P.P.C.S. (Spl) (Mains) 2004

**Q3.** Which one of the following gave the idea of Constituent Assembly for India?

- **A.** Simon Commission
- **B.** Rajaji Formula
- **C.** Cabinet Mission Plan
- **D.** Wavell Plan

**Answer:** C — Cabinet Mission Plan
**Explanation:** Constituent Assembly was founded under Cabinet Mission. The President of Cabinet Mission declared that the main purpose of this mission was to make a Constitution Committee for Constitutional reforms in India. According to the Proposals of the Cabinet Mission, the assembly of the constituent assembly will be constituted by the representatives of the legislative assembly of provinces, the chief commissioners and the representatives of the princely states.
*Asked in:* U.P. U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 2010

**Q4.** Under the Cabinet Mission Plan, the total number of seats allotted to each province in the Constituent Assembly was roughly in the ratio of one representative to the population of -

- **A.** 8 lakh persons
- **B.** 10 lakh persons
- **C.** 11 lakh persons
- **D.** 12 lakh persons

**Answer:** B — 10 lakh persons
**Explanation:** Under the Cabinet Mission, the total number of seats allocated to each province in the Constituent Assembly was roughly in the ratio of one representative to the population of 10 lakh persons on a communal basis. Three classes of voters were accepted - (1) General (2) Muslims (3) Sikhs (only in Punjab).
*Asked in:* U.P.U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 2002; U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2001

**Q5.** The first session of the Constituent Assembly was held on :

- **A.** 16th August, 1947
- **B.** 26th January, 1948
- **C.** 9th December, 1946
- **D.** 26th November, 1946

**Answer:** C — 9th December, 1946
**Explanation:** The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly was held on 9th December, 1946 AD. After two days, Rajendra Prasad was elected as the permanent President of the Constituent Assembly on 11 December, 1946 AD.
*Asked in:* U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2009

**Q6.** Who among the following was the President of the Indian Constituent Assembly?

- **A.** Dr. Rajendra Prasad
- **B.** Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru
- **C.** Sardar Patel
- **D.** Dr. B. R. Ambedkar

**Answer:** A — Dr. Rajendra Prasad
**Explanation:** Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the permanent Chairman of the Indian Constituent Assembly. Dr. B. R. Ambedkar was President of the Drafting Committee. Jawaharlal Nehru was President of Union Power Committee, Union Constitution Committee etc. Vallabhbhai Patel was President of Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities, Tribal and excluded areas.
*Asked in:* U.P.R.O./A.R.O. (Pre) 2014

**Q7.** The first President of the Sovereign Constituent Assembly for the Dominion of India was -

- **A.** C. Rajagopalachari
- **B.** Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
- **C.** Rajendra Prasad
- **D.** Sachchidananda Sinha

**Answer:** C — Rajendra Prasad
**Explanation:** The Constituent Assembly was not sovereign at the time of formation; it was declared sovereign on 15th August, 1947 AD and that day Rajendra Prasad was elected as permanent President of Constituent Assembly. So Rajendra Prasad is the correct answer.
*Asked in:* U.P.P.S.C. (GIC) 2010

**Q8.** Which one of the following statements is correct?

- **A.** The Constituent Assembly of India was elected by the Provincial Assemblies in the year 1946.
- **B.** Jawaharlal Nehru, M.A.Jinnah and Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel were members of the Constituent Assembly of India.
- **C.** The first session of the Constituent Assembly of India was held in January, 1947.
- **D.** The Constitution of India was adopted on 26 January, th 1950.

**Answer:** A — The Constituent Assembly of India was elected by the Provincial Assemblies in the year 1946.
**Explanation:** Under the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946, elections were held for the first time for Constituent Assembly. The elections for the 296 seats assigned to the British Indian provinces were completed by July, 1946 AD. Congress won 208 seats and Muslim League won 73 seats and other independent candidates won 15 seats. M. A. Jinnah was not a member of the Constituent Assembly of India. The Constituent Assembly was the first Parliament of Independent India. Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was the first President (Temporary Chairman of the Assembly) of the Constituent Assembly when it met on December 9, 1946 AD. Dr. Rajendra Prasad then became the permanent Chairman of the Constituent Assembly, and later became the first President of India. The Constitution of India was adopted on 26th November, 1949 AD.
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 2004

**Q9.** Which political party's National Executive called for the dissolution of the Constituent Assembly and its re- election by adult suffrage?

- **A.** Hindu Mahasabha
- **B.** Socialist Party
- **C.** Swaraj Party
- **D.** Muslim League
- **E.** Question not attempted

**Answer:** B — Socialist Party
**Explanation:** The National Executive of the Indian Socialist Party in 1946 A. D. demanded the dissolution of the Constituent Assembly and its re-election through universal adult suffrage. Socialist leaders such as Jayaprakash Narayan and Ram Manohar Lohia argued that the Constituent Assembly, which was indirectly elected by the Provincial Legislatures, did not adequately represent the common Indian people. Therefore, these leaders advocated for a more democratic process and called for the reconstitution of the Constituent Assembly based on universal adult suffrage.
*Asked in:* Rajasthan P.C.S. (Pre) 2024

**Q10.** Sachchidananda Sinha was associated with :

- **A.** Quit India Movement
- **B.** Dandi March
- **C.** Civil Disobedience Movement
- **D.** None of these

**Answer:** A — Quit India Movement
**Explanation:** Sachchidanand Sinha was associated with Quit India Movement. He was elected as temporary Chairman in the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly (9 December, 1946 AD).
*Asked in:* 44th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2000

**Q11.** Who among the following held the Office of Speaker in Central Legislative Assembly of British era and the Parliament of free India?

- **A.** Sir Abdur Rahim
- **B.** G.V. Mavlankar
- **C.** Ananat Shayanam Ayanger
- **D.** Vitthal Bhai Patel

**Answer:** B — G.V. Mavlankar
**Explanation:** G. V. Mavlankar held the office of Speaker of Central Legislative Assembly of British era (24 January 1946 AD to 14 Aug, 1947 AD) and was speaker of Lok Sabha after Independence from 1952 AD to 1956 AD. He was President of Legislative Assembly of Bombay province from 1937 AD to 1946 AD.
*Asked in:* M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2010
