## 50. Partition of India and Independence

**Q1.** Which one of the following parties was in power in the U.K. when India got Independence?

- **A.** Conservative Party
- **B.** Labour Party
- **C.** Liberal Party
- **D.** Socialist Party

**Answer:** B — Labour Party
**Explanation:** During the independence of India, Clement Richard Attlee from Labour party was the Prime Minister of U. K. He was the Prime Minister of U. K. from 1945 to 1951 AD.
*Asked in:* U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2012

**Q2.** Who was the Prime Minister of England when India attained independence?

- **A.** Winston Churchill
- **B.** Clement Attlee
- **C.** Harold Macmillan
- **D.** None of these

**Answer:** B — Clement Attlee
**Explanation:** During the independence of India, Clement Richard Attlee from Labour party was the Prime Minister of U. K. He was the Prime Minister of U. K. from 1945 to 1951 AD.
*Asked in:* Chhattisgarh P.C.S. (Pre) 2003

**Q3.** The British Government decided and declared to leave India by June, 1948 in :

- **A.** 1946
- **B.** February, 1947
- **C.** April, 1947
- **D.** June, 1947

**Answer:** B — February, 1947
**Explanation:** Prime Minister of Britain Attlee declared in the House of Commons on February, 20, 1947 AD that British will leave India before June, 1948 AD, after transferring power to liable people. Attlee appointed Lord Mountbatten as the Viceroy of India in place of Wavell. Mountbatten initiated the efforts of power transfer in March, 1947 AD.
*Asked in:* Uttarakhand P.C.S. (Mains) 2006

**Q4.** Lord Mountbatten came to India as a Viceroy along with specific instruction to -

- **A.** Balkanize the Indian sub-continent
- **B.** Keep India United if possible
- **C.** Accept Jinnah's demand for Pakistan
- **D.** Persuade the Congress to accept partition

**Answer:** B — Keep India United if possible
**Explanation:** The Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, Clement Attlee announced on 20th February, 1947 AD in the House of Commons that he wish to transfer powers to India but also said that if in time the decision related to the constitution is not made British Empire has the power to transfer Government to any of them. Thus, to effect the transfer of power, Attlee decided to send Lord Mountbatten as Viceroy to India. Lord Mountbatten armed with vast powers became India's Viceroy on 24 March, 1947 AD. Mountbatten became Viceroy of India with a mandate to oversee the British withdrawal. Lord Mountbatten came to India as Viceroy of India along with specifi c instructions to keep India United if possible however he was authorized to make decisions according to favourable Indian circumstances and minimum British loss. Mountbatten concluded that a United India was an unachievable goal and resigned himself to a plan for partition, creating the independent nations of India and Pakistan.
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 1998

**Q5.** On February 20, 1947, Prime Minister Attlee announced the British Government's decision to withdraw from India latest by

- **A.** June 1948
- **B.** August 1947
- **C.** January 1948
- **D.** More than one of the above
- **E.** None of the above

**Answer:** A — June 1948
**Explanation:** On 20 February, 1947 AD British Prime Minister Clement Attlee, announced in the House of Commons that the British would leave India before 30 June, 1948. AD Hence option (a) is correct.
*Asked in:* 68th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2022

**Q6.** Which plan became the platform of Indian Independence?

- **A.** Cripps Plan
- **B.** Wavell Plan
- **C.** Mountbatten Plan
- **D.** None of the above

**Answer:** C — Mountbatten Plan
**Explanation:** Lord Mountbatten came to India in March, 1947 AD with the purpose to give complete independence to India. He decided 15 August, 1947 AD as the date for power transfer. He made a plan of partition of India under instructions of Attlee which was considered as Mountbatten Plan.
*Asked in:* U.P. U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 2006

**Q7.** The Mountbatten Plan became the basis for :

- **A.** Continuity of British Rule.
- **B.** Transfer of power.
- **C.** Partition of the country.
- **D.** Solution of communal problems.

**Answer:** B, C — Transfer of power.; Partition of the country.
**Explanation:** Lord Mountbatten came to India in March, 1947 AD with the purpose to give complete independence to India. He decided 15 August, 1947 AD as the date for power transfer. He made a plan of partition of India under instructions of Attlee which was considered as Mountbatten Plan.
*Asked in:* U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2013

**Q8.** Which Act provided for the partition of India into two new dominions - India and Pakistan?

- **A.** Govt. of India Act, 1919
- **B.** Govt. of India Act, 1935
- **C.** Indian Independence Act, 1947
- **D.** None of the above

**Answer:** C — Indian Independence Act, 1947
**Explanation:** • The Indian Independence Act, 1947, passed by the British Parliament, formally approved the partition of British India and provided the legal basis for the creation of two new independent dominions-India and Pakistan. • This Act received Royal Assent on 18 July 1947, and under its provisions, India and Pakistan came into existence as two independent dominions on 15 August 1947.
*Asked in:* 71st B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2025

**Q9.** The British Parliament passed the Indian Independence Act in -

- **A.** January, 1947
- **B.** July, 1947
- **C.** August, 1947
- **D.** August, 1946

**Answer:** B — July, 1947
**Explanation:** As per the Mountbatten Plan (June 3, 1947 AD), British Parliament passed the Indian Independence Act on July, 1947 AD. The bill received Royal Assent of his majesty on 18 July, 1947 AD. In this Act, India and Pakistan were decided as two dominion States with effect from 15 August, 1947 AD.
*Asked in:* U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2012; Uttarakhand U.D.A./ L.D.A. (Pre) 2007

**Q10.** The Indian Independence Act, 1947 came into force on -

- **A.** July 4, 1947
- **B.** July 10, 1947
- **C.** July 18, 1947
- **D.** August 14, 1947

**Answer:** C — July 18, 1947
**Explanation:** As per the Mountbatten Plan (June 3, 1947 AD), British Parliament passed the Indian Independence Act on July, 1947 AD. The bill received Royal Assent of his majesty on 18 July, 1947 AD. In this Act, India and Pakistan were decided as two dominion States with effect from 15 August, 1947 AD.
*Asked in:* U.P.R.O./ A.R.O. (Pre) 2014

**Q11.** The formula for transfer of sovereignty to India in 1947 was known as -

- **A.** Durand Plan
- **B.** Morley-Minto Reforms
- **C.** Mountbatten Plan
- **D.** Wavell Plan

**Answer:** C — Mountbatten Plan
**Explanation:** As per the Mountbatten Plan (June 3, 1947 AD), British Parliament passed the Indian Independence Act on July, 1947 AD. The bill received Royal Assent of his majesty on 18 July, 1947 AD. In this Act, India and Pakistan were decided as two dominion States with effect from 15 August, 1947 AD.
*Asked in:* U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1994

**Q12.** "Mountbatten Plan" regarding the partition of India was officially declared on :

- **A.** June 04, 1947
- **B.** June 10, 1947
- **C.** July 03, 1947
- **D.** June 03, 1947

**Answer:** D — June 03, 1947
**Explanation:** Mountbatten Plan regarding the partition of India was officially declared on June 3, 1947 AD. The British Government accorded formal approval to the Mountbatten Plan by enacting the Indian Independence Act.
*Asked in:* M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2014

**Q13.** Assertion (A) : Britain made India free in 1947. Reason (R) : Britain had become weak during the second World War. In the context of the above two statements, which of the following is/are correct? Code :

- **A.** Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
- **B.** Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not a correct explanation of (A).
- **C.** (A) is true, but (R) is false.
- **D.** (A) is false, but (R) is true.

**Answer:** A — Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
**Explanation:** Assertion (A) and Reason (R) both are correct and (R) is correct explanation of (A). Britishers were weak after the Second World War and after evaluating the National Movement of India it is clear that people of various castes, religions, organisations and parties contributed to the independence.
*Asked in:* U.P. P.S.C. (GIC) 2010; U.P. Lower Sub.(Spl.) (Pre) 2003; U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2001

**Q14.** Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labeled as Reason (R). Assertion (A) : The British sovereignty continued to exist in free India. Reason (R) : The British sovereign appointed the last Governor-General of free India. In the context of the above two statements, which one of the following is correct? Code :

- **A.** Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
- **B.** Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
- **C.** (A) is true, but (R) is false.
- **D.** (A) is false, but (R) is true.

**Answer:** D — (A) is false, but (R) is true.
**Explanation:** The Indian Independence Act was presented in the House of Commons in British Parliament on July 4, 1947 AD. It received royal assent on July 18, 1947 AD. According to its provisions, the British Government would not continue any control over any dominion from 15 August,1947 AD. The second statement is correct as British Sovereign appointed the last Governor-General of free India. Thus, Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 1996

**Q15.** The Indian Independence Bill received the Royal Assent on -

- **A.** July 18 , 1947
- **B.** July 19 , 1947 th th
- **C.** July 20 , 1947
- **D.** July 21, 1947 th st

**Answer:** A — July 18 , 1947
**Explanation:** The Indian Independence Act of 1947 was an implementation of the Mountbatten Plan. The Indian Independence Act was presented in the House of commons of British Parliament on July 4, 1947 AD by the then Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, Clement Attlee. The Indian Independence Act was passed by the House of Commons on July 15, 1947 AD and next day by the House of Lords. Finally, it received royal assent on July 18, 1947 AD.
*Asked in:* U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2014

**Q16.** The Balkan Plan for fragmentation of India was the brain child of -

- **A.** W. Churchill
- **B.** M.A. Jinnah
- **C.** Lord Mountbatten
- **D.** V.P. Menon

**Answer:** C — Lord Mountbatten
**Explanation:** After arriving in India to negotiate terms for an Independent India, Mountbatten soon concluded that transfer of power to one central representative constituency assembly for India would be impossible to achieve as neither the India National Congress nor the Muslim League could agree to the terms, and he accordingly came up with 'Plan Balkan', separate dominion for Pakistan, the Princely States and the rest of British India with certain key areas of administration run by Central Government.
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 2000

**Q17.** The Indian National Congress agreed in 1947 to the partition of the country mainly because -

- **A.** The principle of Two-Nation Theory was then acceptable to them.
- **B.** It was imposed by the British Government and the Congress was helpless in this regard.
- **C.** They wanted to avoid large-scale communal riots.
- **D.** India would have otherwise lost the opportunity to attain freedom.

**Answer:** C — They wanted to avoid large-scale communal riots.
**Explanation:** Attlee announced the appointment of Lord Mountbatten as Viceroy replacing Lord Wavell. Lord Mountbatten, the last British Governor-General and Viceroy arrived in India in March, 1947 AD and immediately began to take measures for the transfer of power. The prevailing communal violence in the country led Mountbatten to announce the partition plan on 3rd June, 1947 AD. The Congress leaders too had come to the conclusion that partition was the only choice to check the widespread communal violence and bloodshed that was ravaging the country. The plan provided for the immediate transfer of power on the basis of the grant of Dominion Status. The Indian National Congress agreed to the partition of the Country mainly because they wanted to avoid large-scale communal riots.
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 1998

**Q18.** Assertion (A) : The Indian National Congress accepted the Mountbatten plan. Reason (R) : It believed in Two-Nation Theory. Select the correct answer from the code given below: Code :

- **A.** Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
- **B.** Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
- **C.** (A) is true, but (R) is false.
- **D.** (A) is false, but (R) is true.

**Answer:** C — (A) is true, but (R) is false.
**Explanation:** Assertion (A) is correct, but reason (R) is wrong as though INC accepted Mountbatten plan, but they never accepted 'Two Nation Theory.' The reason behind their acceptance of the Mountbatten Plan was to avoid communal riots in the country.
*Asked in:* U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1998

**Q19.** As an alternative to the partition of India, Gandhiji suggested to Mountbatten that he -

- **A.** Postpone granting of independence.
- **B.** Invite Jinnah to form the Government.
- **C.** Invite Nehru and Jinnah to form the Government together.
- **D.** Invite the army to take over for some time.

**Answer:** B — Invite Jinnah to form the Government.
**Explanation:** The first meeting between Gandhiji and Mountbatten took place on 31st March, 1947 AD. As an alternative to the partition of India, Gandhiji suggested to Mountbatten that the best course would be to ask Jinnah to take over as Prime Minister of Interim Government and run the affairs of the Country but this suggestion of Gandhiji was not acceptable to Congress Leaders and Congress Working Committee. He told his attendants: "Today I find myself all alone. Even Sardar and Jawaharlal think that he was wrong, and peace was sure to return if the partition was agreed upon. Nevertheless, I must speak as I feel... we may not feel the full impact immediately, but, I can see clearly that the future of independence gained at this price is going to be dark. Should the evil I apprehend overtake India... let posterity know what agony this old soul went through, thinking of it.... Let it not be said that Gandhi was party to Indian vivisection."
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 2000

**Q20.** The Radcliffe Committee was appointed to -

- **A.** Solve the problem of minorities in India.
- **B.** Give effect to the Independence Bill.
- **C.** Demarcate the boundaries between India and Pakistan.
- **D.** Enquire into the riots in East Bengal.

**Answer:** C — Demarcate the boundaries between India and Pakistan.
**Explanation:** Viceroy of British India, Lord Mountbatten formed two commissions namely Punjab Border Commission and Bengal Border Commission to decide the borderline between India and Pakistan on June 30, 1947 AD. Cyril Radcliffe was appointed as President of both the Commissions. Those Commissions had to demarcate borders by Muslims and Non-Muslims population. They had to consider other factors too. There were four members (judges) in each Commission of which two were from Indian National Congress and two from the Muslim League.
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 2014

**Q21.** Who headed the Boundary Commission appointed in 1947 in the context of India's partition?

- **A.** Mountbatten
- **B.** Radcliffe
- **C.** James Bolt
- **D.** Richardson

**Answer:** B — Radcliffe
**Explanation:** Viceroy of British India, Lord Mountbatten formed two commissions namely Punjab Border Commission and Bengal Border Commission to decide the borderline between India and Pakistan on June 30, 1947 AD. Cyril Radcliffe was appointed as President of both the Commissions. Those Commissions had to demarcate borders by Muslims and Non-Muslims population. They had to consider other factors too. There were four members (judges) in each Commission of which two were from Indian National Congress and two from the Muslim League.
*Asked in:* U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2015

**Q22.** Who among the following headed the two Boundary Commissions set up to delineate the international frontiers between India and Pakistan in 1947?

- **A.** Cyril Radcliffe
- **B.** A.P. Moon
- **C.** A.V. Alexander
- **D.** More than one of the above
- **E.** None of the above

**Answer:** A — Cyril Radcliffe
**Explanation:** Bengal and Punjab boundary commissions were established in 1947 AD under chairmanship of British lawyer Cyril Radcliffe for the purpose of determining new border between India and Pakistan following independence from British rule. The Radcliffe line became the border between India and Pakistan when the Award was published on 17 August 1947, two days after partition.
*Asked in:* 68th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2022

**Q23.** The last opportunity to avoid the partition of India was lost with the rejection of:

- **A.** Cripps Mission
- **B.** Rajagopalachari Formula
- **C.** Cabinet Mission
- **D.** Wavell Plan

**Answer:** C — Cabinet Mission
**Explanation:** The Cabinet Mission of India of 1946 AD had come up with a plan on 16 May, 1946 AD which intended to create a United India with independent Muslim and Hindu majority provinces in which demand of Pakistan raised by Muslim League was rejected, but Muslim League approved the plan on 6th June,1946 AD. On July 29, it rejected the plan and called the Muslims to resort to "Direct Action" to achieve the land of their dream "Pakistan." August 16, 1946 AD was fixed as "Direct Action Day." As a result, the last opportunity to avoid the partition of India was lost with the rejection of Cabinet Mission.
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 2002

## 51. Constitutional Development of India

**Q1.** The Regulating Act was passed in -

- **A.** 1773
- **B.** 1774
- **C.** 1785
- **D.** 1793

**Answer:** A — 1773
**Explanation:** Regulating Act, 1773, was passed by the British Parliament for the regulation of the British East India Company's Indian Territories, mainly in Bengal. The main provisions of the Act were the appointment of a Governor-General of Fort William in Bengal with supervisory powers over the Presidencies of Madras (now Chennai) and Bombay (now Mumbai). The Governor-General had a Council of four who were given the power to cast a vote but no veto. Warren Hastings was appointed the first Governor General of Bengal.
*Asked in:* 39th B.P.S.C. (Pre) 1994

**Q5.** The Supreme Court was set up for the first time in India under the:

**Answer:** A — Regulating Act, 1773
**Explanation:** The Regulating Act, (1773), established India's first Supreme Court, at Fort William, Calcutta. This Supreme Court consisted of a Chief Justice and three other regular Judges or Puisne Judges. Sir Elijah Impey was the first Chief Justice. The Supreme Court was the supreme judiciary over all British subjects including the provinces of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa. The Supreme Court came into force in 1774 AD.

**Q10.** By a Regulation in 1793, the District Collector was deprived of his judicial powers and made the collecting agent only. What was the reason for such regulation?

- **A.** Lord Cornwallis felt that the District Collector's efficiency of revenue collection would enormously increase without the burden of other work.
- **B.** Lord Cornwallis felt that judicial power should compulsorily be in the hands of Europeans. While Indians could be given the job of revenue collection in the districts.
- **C.** Lord Cornwallis was alarmed at the extent of power concentrated in the District Collector and felt that such absolute power was undesirable in one person.
- **D.** The judicial work demanded a deep knowledge of India and a good training in law and Lord Cornwallis felt that District Collector should be only a revenue collector.

**Answer:** C — Lord Cornwallis was alarmed at the extent of power concentrated in the District Collector and felt that such absolute power was undesirable in one person.
**Explanation:** Cornwallis judicial reforms took their final shape in 1793 AD and were embodied in the famous Cornwallis Code. The new reforms were based on the principle of Separation of Powers. Under the influence of the eighteenth-century French philosophers Cornwallis sought to separate the revenue administration from the administration of justice. The Collector was the head of the revenue department in a district and also enjoyed extensive judicial and magisterial powers. Cornwallis believed that concentration of all powers in the hands of the Collector in the District retards the improvement as a judge of the Diwani Adalat redress the wrongs done by him as collector or assessor of revenue? Thus, neither the landlords nor the cultivators could regard the Collector as an impartial Judge in revenue cases. The Cornwallis Code divested the Collector of all judicial and magisterial powers and left him with the duty of administration of revenue. A new class of officer called the District Judge was created to preside over the District Civil Court. The District Judge was empowered with magisterial and police functions.
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 2010

**Q15.** Which of the following is one of the reasons for considering the Charter Act of 1813 important for India?

- **D.** It approved the development of a railway system in India.

**Q16.** Which one of the following provisions was not made in the Charter Act of 1833?

- **A.** The trading activities of the East India Company were to be abolished.
- **B.** The designation of the supreme authority was to be changed as the Governor General of India-in-Council.
- **C.** All law-making powers to be conferred on Governor- General-in-council.
- **D.** An Indian was to be appointed as a Law Member of the Governor-General's Council.

**Answer:** D — An Indian was to be appointed as a Law Member of the Governor-General's Council.
**Explanation:** The Charter Act, 1833, was renewed on the condition that Company should abandon its trade entirely, both with India and China and permit Europeans to settle freely in India. The Company lost its monopoly in China and also the trade of tea which it enjoyed with the Charter Act of 1813. GovernorGeneral of Bengal was made the Governor-General of British India with this Act, and all financial and administrative powers were centralized in the hands of Governor-Generalin-Council. The 4 member was not entitled to act as a th member of the Council except for legislative purposes. A British member was appointed as a Law Member in the Governor-General's Council. A first fourth person appointed as the Member of the Council was Lord Macaulay. Thus option (d) is the correct answer.
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 2003

**Q17.** By which one of the following Acts was the Governor General of Bengal designated as the Governor General of India?

- **B.** The Pitt's India Act
- **C.** The Charter Act of 1793
- **D.** The Charter Act of 1833

**Answer:** D — The Charter Act of 1833
**Explanation:** The Charter Act, 1833, was renewed on the condition that Company should abandon its trade entirely, both with India and China and permit Europeans to settle freely in India. The Company lost its monopoly in China and also the trade of tea which it enjoyed with the Charter Act of 1813. GovernorGeneral of Bengal was made the Governor-General of British India with this Act, and all financial and administrative powers were centralized in the hands of Governor-Generalin-Council. The 4 member was not entitled to act as a th member of the Council except for legislative purposes. A British member was appointed as a Law Member in the Governor-General's Council. A first fourth person appointed as the Member of the Council was Lord Macaulay. Thus option (d) is the correct answer.
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 2023

**Q18.** Which of the among following had recommended to hold the Indian Civil Service Examination simultaneously in India & England?

**Explanation:** The Montagu-Chelmsford Report recommended to increase the number of Indians in administration and also recommended that the examination shall be jointly held in Britain and India for Civil Services. On their recommendation, the Civil Services was held simultaneously in England and India from 1922 AD. The Aitchison Commission submitted its report in 1887 AD. The Commission opposed to the demand of the simultaneous holding, in England as well as in India.

The number of the Directors of the Court of Directors was re duced from 24 to 18 of whom 6 were to be nominated by the Crown. The Court of Directors was divested of its right to patronage and Company's services were thrown open to competition and no dis crimination of any kind was to be made. A Committee with Macau lay was formed in the following year (1854) to give effect to the scheme of appointment in Civil Services through competition.

**Q21.** In which of the following years the British Government finally agreed to hold the Indian Civil Services (I.C.S.) examination simultaneously in India and England?

**Q22.** With reference to Indian Civil Services, which of the following statement/s is/are correct? 1. **Q29.** Which of the following Acts transferred the Government of India from East India Company to the Crown?

**Answer:** C — The Government of India Act, 1858
**Explanation:** British Parliament tabled the Government of India Act, 1858, which transferred powers from the East India Company to the Crown. A member of the British Parliament was made Secretary of State for India exercise powers on behalf of the Crown and was responsible to the British Parliament, assisted by the Advisory Council of India. **Q44.** In which Constitutional document was Dyarchy System introduced in Indian provinces?

- **A.** 1892
- **B.** 1909
- **C.** 1919
- **D.** 1935

**Answer:** C — 1919
**Explanation:** The Montagu-Chelmsford Reform of 1919 was introduced by the British Government in India to introduce self-governing institutions gradually to India. In this 'Dyarchy in the Provinces' was introduced. Reserved subjects like Finance, Law and order, Army, Police, etc. and Transferred subjects like Public health, education, agriculture, Local Self-Government, etc. were included The reserved subjects were kept with the Governor and his executive council. While the administration of the transferred subjects was handed over to the ministers responsible to the Provincial Legislature.

**Q50.** Consider the following statements - Assertion (A) : The structure and characteristics of governance remained unitary and central with enforcement of the Government of India Act of 1919. Reason ( R) : A large part of authority was delegated to Provinces. Which of the following is correct in the reference of the above?

- **A.** Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
- **B.** Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
- **C.** (A) is true, but (R) is false.
- **D.** (A) is false, but (R) is true.

**Answer:** D — (A) is false, but (R) is true.
**Explanation:** The Government of India Act of 1919 introduced dyarchy system in provinces. Education, Local Self-Government, Medical Relief, Public Health and Sanitation, Agriculture, Cooperative Societies, Public Works, Excise, Justice, Police, Irrigation and Waterways, Labour, Welfare and Industrial Disputes, etc. 50 subjects were delegated to Provinces. On the other hand, Central Legislative had rights over 47 subjects such as Defence, Foreign Affairs, Money communication, etc. Although Governor-General had major executive powers but the structure and characteristics of governance were generally, federal. Thus, statement (A) is wrong and Reason (R) is correct.
*Asked in:* U.P. U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 1998

**Q51.** Consider the following statements - Assertion (A) : Dyarchy means division of administrative affairs in two sections. Reason ( R) : It was introduced for enforcement of responsible governance in Provinces. Which of the following is correct in the reference of the above?

- **A.** Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
- **B.** Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
- **C.** (A) is true, but (R) is false.
- **D.** (A) is false, but (R) is true.

**Answer:** A — Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
**Explanation:** The Government of India Act, 1919 made a major change in Provincial governance. The Government of India Act, 1919 introduced the system of Dyarchy. Dyarchy means a dual set of Governments. The Government of India Act of 1919, made a provision for classification of the central and provincial subjects. The provincial subjects were divided into two groups: one was Reserved and another was Transferred. The Reserved subjects were kept with the Governor and his executive council and transferred subjects were handed over to the Minister responsible to the provincial legislature. This division of subjects was basically what they meant by introducing the Dyarchy.
*Asked in:* U.P. U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 1998

**Q55.** Which of the following report was the baseline of the Government of India Act, 1935?

- **B.** 1 and 2
- **C.** 2 and 3
- **D.** 1, 2 and 3

**Q58.** Which of the following was not one of the features of the Government of India Act, 1935?

- **A.** Reconstruction of the Governor General's Executive Council
- **B.** Provincial Autonomy
- **C.** Appraisal of the Act of 1935
- **D.** Proposal for Federation of India

**Answer:** C — Appraisal of the Act of 1935
**Explanation:** The Government of India Act, 1935, introduced several key reforms: (a) The Governor-General's Executive Council was restructured to include more Indian members, though the Governor-General retained ultimate authority. (b) Provincial Autonomy granted provinces more independence in certain administrative areas, though the Governor still held significant powers. (c) The Act itself was a legislative framework and did not include any provision for its appraisal. (d) The Act proposed a federation that would incorporate both British India and princely states, but it was never fully implemented due to the princely states' refusal to join.

**Explanation:** The Government of India Act, 1935, introduced several key reforms: (a) The Governor-General's Executive Council was restructured to include more Indian members, though the Governor-General retained ultimate authority. (b) Provincial Autonomy granted provinces more independence in certain administrative areas, though the Governor still held significant powers. (c) The Act itself was a legislative framework and did not include any provision for its appraisal. (d) The Act proposed a federation that would incorporate both British India and princely states, but it was never fully implemented due to the princely states' refusal to join.
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 2000

**Q62.** The real intention of the British to include the Princely States in the Federal Union proposed by the India Act of 1935 was to -

- **A.** Exercise more direct political and administrative control.
- **B.** Involve the princes actively in the administration of the colony.
- **C.** Finally effect the complete political and administrative take-over of all the princely States by the British
- **D.** Use the princes to counter-balance the anti-imperialist doctrines of the nationalist leaders.

**Answer:** D — Use the princes to counter-balance the anti-imperialist doctrines of the nationalist leaders.
**Explanation:** The real intention of the British to include the Princely States in the Federal Union proposed by the India Act of 1935 was to use the princes to counter balance the antiimperialist doctrines of the nationalist leaders. Princely States represented approx 25% of the population of India while under the Government of India Act, 1935 out of 260 members 156 were to represent the provinces and 104 to the Princely States in the Upper House and the Lower House consisted of 375 members out of whom 250 were to represent the provinces and 125 to represent the Princely States. In both Houses of the Federal Legislature, the states were given their quota of representation. But the members from the State were not to be elected. Despite such a wide range of provisions, the princely states however refused to join the Federation. They were alarmed by the changing situation in the country caused by the rapid spread of the National Movement. The British Government miserably failed to overcome the opposition of the Indian National Congress, the Muslim League and the princes against the Federal Scheme. So the Federal Scheme was withheld except the establishment of the Federal Court and the Provincial scheme was introduced on 1st April, 1937 causing a drastic change in the pattern of provincial politics.
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 2002

## 52. Modern History : Miscellaneous

**Q1.** Consider the following statements: 1. Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General who established a regular police force in India on the British pattern. 2. A Supreme Court was established at Calcutta by the Regulating Act, 1773. 3. The Indian Penal Code came into effect in the year 1860. Which of the statements given above are correct?

- **A.** 1 and 2
- **B.** 2 and 3
- **C.** 1 and 3
- **D.** 1, 2 and 3

**Answer:** B — 2 and 3
**Explanation:** Lord Cornwallis was the first Governor-General who established a regular police force in India on the British pattern. Thus, statement 1 is wrong. The Regulating Act of 1773 established a Supreme Court at Fort William, Calcutta. Thus, statement 2 is correct. The Indian Penal Code (IPC) was drafted in 1860 on the recommendations of first law commission. Thus statement 3 is also correct. Thus, option (b) is the correct answer.

**Q9.** Which of the following famines of the 19 century in th India has been described as 'Sea of Calamity'?

- **D.** Orissa Famine of 1866-67

**Answer:** D — Orissa Famine of 1866-67
**Explanation:** Orissa (Odisha) Famine of 1866-67 AD in India has been described as 'Sea of Calamity.' The impact of the famine, however, was greatest in Odisha, which at that time was quite isolated from the rest of India. In Odisha alone, at least 1.3 million (13 lakh) people, a third of the population died in 1866 due to starvation and diseases.

- **D.** Indigo Commission

**Q11.** Which of the following commissions are related to famine in British India ? 1. Campbell Commission 2. Lyall Commission 3. Strachey Commission 4. Hunter Commission Select the correct answer from the code given below :

- **A.** Only 1, 2 and 3
- **B.** Only 1, 2 and 4
- **C.** Only 1, 3 and 4
- **D.** All 1, 2, 3 and 4

**Answer:** A — Only 1, 2 and 3
**Explanation:** 1. Campbell Commission - This commission was constituted in 1866, to investigate the causes of famine (especially in connection with the then Orissa famine) and to suggest measures for prevention and relief. 2. Lyall Commission - This commission examined famine conditions and suggested relief-related measures (it is associated with the famine inquiry after the 1896-97 famine). 3. Strachey Commission - This commission was constituted after the Great Famine (1876-78) to frame policy and principles for dealing with famines and became an important basis for famine relief planning/codes. 4. Hunter Commission - This commission was not a famine commission; it was mainly related to education (and "Hunter Commission" is also used for a later inquiry of a different context).
*Asked in:* Uttarakhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2025

**Q13.** Which of the following pairs are correctly matched? List- I (Period) List- II A. AD 1767 - 69 1. First Anglo-Maratha War B. AD 1790 - 92 2. Third Mysore War C. AD 1824 - 26 3. First Anglo-Burmese War D. AD 1845 - 46 4. Second Sikh War Code :

- **A.** 2 and 4
- **B.** 3 and 4
- **C.** 1 and 2
- **D.** 2 and 3

**Answer:** D — 2 and 3
**Explanation:** First Anglo-Maratha War (1775-82 AD) - The internal problems of the Marathas and the growing ambition of the English brought the beginning of the Anglo-Maratha struggle. The primary cause of the first Maratha war was the interference of the English Government at Bombay in the internal affairs of the Marathas. The First Anglo-Maratha War ended with the Treaty of Salbai signed between the Mahadaji Scindia and the Warren Hastings in 1782 AD. In the Treaty of Salbai, status quo was maintained which gave the British 20 years of peace with the Marathas. Third Anglo- Mysore War (1790-92 AD)- It was fought between British and Tipu Sultan. British attacked Srirangapatnam with the help of Nizam and Marathas. Under the leadership of William Medows, British defeated Tipu Sultan and they had a treaty in Srirangapatnam in March, 1792 AD. According to this treaty, Tipu Sultan was to give away half of his kingdom and he had to pay 3 crores to British for damages done in the war. The First Anglo-Burmese War (1824-26 AD) - The first of three wars fought between the British and Burmese Empires in the 19th century. The war which began primarily over the control of northeastern India, ended in a decisive British victory, giving the total British control of Assam, Manipur, Cachar and Jaintia as well as Arakan Province and Tenasserim. The Burmese were also forced to pay an indemnity of one million pounds, and sign a commercial treaty 'Treaty of Yandabo'. Second Anglo-Sikh War (1848-49 AD)-The Second AngloSikh War took place in 1848 and 1849 between the Sikh Empire and the British East India Company.
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 2004

**Q14.** Consider the following events and arrange them in chronological order from earliest to latest: 1. Vellore Mutiny 2. Death of Nana Phadnavis 3. Recall of Wellesley 4. Anglo-Nepalese War Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

- **A.** 2, 3, 1, 4
- **B.** 4, 1, 3, 2
- **C.** 2, 3, 4, 1
- **D.** 3, 1, 2, 4

**Answer:** A — 2, 3, 1, 4
**Explanation:** On July 10, 1806 AD, a military uprising took place at the Vellore Fort in Tamil Nadu, known as the Vellore Mutiny. The mutiny was caused by several social, religious, and political factors, particularly British policies and their disregard for Indian soldiers' sentiments. Nana Phadnavis, a prominent political leader of the Maratha society, passed away in March 1800 AD. Lord Wellesley served as Governor-General from 1798 AD to 1805 AD. Due to his aggressive expansionist policies and military campaigns, the British government faced financial difficulties and recalled him in 1805 AD. Lord Hastings (1813-1823 AD) later oversaw the AngloNepalese War (1814-1816 AD), which concluded with the Treaty of Sugauli.
*Asked in:* U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2024

**Q15.** Consider the following events of Modern Indian His- tory 1. Death sentence to Raja Nand Kumar 2. Treaty of Salbai 3. Battle of Wandiwash 4. Death of Tipu Sultan Which of the following is the correct chronological order of the above events?

Death sentence awarded to Raja Nandkumar (1775) - Raja Nandkumar, a hindu Brahmin and former landlord of Berhampur, was tried on charges of forgery and hanged at Calcutta. Treaty of Salbai (1782) - The agreement between the East India Company and the Marathas at the end of the First Anglo- Maratha War (1775-1782) is called the Treaty of Salbai. Death of Tipu Sultan (1799) - Tipu Sultan, the ruler of Mysore, was killed during the Battle of Srirangapatnam in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1799).

**Q17.** Which of the following events was the last in chronological order?

- **B.** Khilafat Movement
- **C.** Home Rule Movement
- **D.** Jallianwala Bagh Massacre

**Answer:** A — Moplah Revolt
**Explanation:** Moplah Revolt (1921 AD) - was the culmination of a series of riots by Mappila Muslims of Kerala in the 19th and early 20th centuries against the British and the Hindu landlords in Malabar. Khilafat Movement (1919-24 AD): The Khilafat Movement, (1919-24 AD) was a movement of Indian Muslims, led by Muhammad Ali and Shaukat Ali and supported by Mahatma Gandhi. Home Rule Movement (1916 AD) - was started in April 1916 AD and September 1916 AD, respectively, by Indian nationalist Bal Gangadhar Tilak and British social reformer Annie Besant. Jallianwala Bagh Massacre (April 13, 1919 AD) - incident occurred on April 13, 1919 AD, in which British troops fired on a large crowd of unarmed Indians in an open space known as the Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar in the Punjab region (now in Punjab state) of India, killing thousands people and wounding many thousands more. Hence option (a) is correct answer.

**Q20.** Match the correctly - A. Child marriage 1. Ishwarchand Vidyasagar B. Suppression of 2. Colonel Sleimen Thuggee C. Widows' Remarriage 3. M.G. Ranade D. Suppression of 4. Lord Hastings Pindaris Code : A B C D

- **A.** 3 2 1 4
- **B.** 4 2 1 3
- **C.** 1 4 3 2
- **D.** 2 3 1 4

**Answer:** A — 3 2 1 4
**Explanation:** Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar is considered one of the pillars of the Bengal Renaissance. In other words, he managed to continue the reforms movement that was started by Raja Rammohan Roy. Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar initiated the concept of Widow Remarriage and he also opened the doors of colleges and other educational institutions to lower caste students, which were earlier reserved only for Brahmins. For his immense generosity and kind-heartedness, people started addressing him as "Daya Sagar" (ocean of kindness). MajorGeneral Sir William Henry Sleeman was a British soldier and administrator in British India, best known for his work on suppression of thuggee. Justice Mahadev Govind Ranade was a judge, politician, writer and reformer of India. He was also an active reformer. He set up the Social Conference Movement, which worked against child marriage, Widows Remarriage, spending heavily in marriages and other social functions. Ranade advocated for widow remarriage and female education. Lord Hastings became Governor-General in 1813. Lord Hastings finally decided to suppress the Pindaris. Hastings planned vigorous military preparations to surround the Pindaris from all sides - on the north and east from Bengal, on the west from Gujarat and the south from the Deccan. A massive army of 113,000 men and 300 cannons was divided into two parts - on the northern side under Hastings' command and the southern under the control of Thomas Hislop. By the end of 1817, the British troops were successful in expelling the Pindaris from Malwa and across the Chambal. In January, 1818 the Pindaris were practically exterminated.
*Asked in:* U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 1990

**Q33.** With reference to Lala Lajpat Rai which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. - **A.** 1 only
- **B.** 2 only
- **C.** Both 1 and 2
- **D.** Neither 1 nor 2

**Answer:** C — Both 1 and 2
**Explanation:** Initially Lala Lajpat Rai was not in favour of the noncooperation movement, because he was not satisfied with the policies of prayer, persuasion and humility of the Congress. But later in September 1920 AD, the Congress held a special session in Calcutta under the leadership of Lala Lajpat Rai and a resolution was passed to run the Non-cooperation Movement. Hence statement 1 is true. The Non-cooperation Movement was called off by Gandhiji on February 4, 1922 AD after Chauri Chaura incident. Angered by incident C. R. Das and Pandit Moti Lal Nehru formed the Swaraj Party in January 1923 AD. Lala Lajpat Rai also joined this party but in June 1925 AD after death of C. R. Das, Lala Lajpat Rai and Pandit Madan Mohan Malviya left the party. Hence both statements are true.

**Q49.** Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Most of the early nationalists considered British rule as an act of providence destined to bring modernisation. Reason (R): They complained only against "Un-British rule" in India. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

- **A.** Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
- **B.** (A) is false, but (R) is true.
- **C.** Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
- **D.** (A) is true, but (R) is false.

**Answer:** C — Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
**Explanation:** A significant portion of the early nationalist leaders viewed British rule in India as a tool ordained by divine will (Providence), which was necessary to bring modernization to India. They believed that British rule facilitated industrialization, education, administrative facilities, and other reforms that paved the way for the development of Indian society. However, their criticism was limited to the "Un-British rule" in India, rather than British rule as a whole. Thus, both the Assertion (A) and the Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) also correctly explains Assertion (A).
*Asked in:* U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2024

**Q55.** With reference to Indian freedom struggle, which one of the following statements in not correct?

- **A.** The Rowlatt Act aroused a wave of popular indignation and led to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre

- **C.** Bhagat Singh was one of the founders of Hindustan Republican Socialist Association
- **D.** In 1931, the Congress Session at Karachi opposed Gandhi-Irwin Pact

**Answer:** D — In 1931, the Congress Session at Karachi opposed Gandhi-Irwin Pact
**Explanation:** The First Round Table Conference could not produce any fruitful result. The main reason was the absence of Congress from the Conference. The Government started to convince the Congress to participate in the Second Round Table Conference in 1931 AD. Finally, Gandhiji was convinced to negotiate with the Viceroy Lord Irwin. So Gandhiji and Lord Irwin met on February 19th, 1931 and after discussion of fifteen days, they signed an agreement on March 5, 1931 th known as "Gandhi-Irwin Pact." In 1931, the Congress session at Karachi, approved the Gandhi-Irwin Pact. Thus, statement (d) is incorrect.

**Q65.** Consider the following statements: 1. The Arya Samaj was founded in 1875. 2. 'Al Hilal' was published by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad. 3. **Q68.** Which one of the following is not correctly matched? Person Associated with

**Explanation:** James Augustus Hicky started a weekly newspaper in 1780 named "Hicky's Bengal Gazette" (also known as "The Original Calcutta General Advertiser"). He was not associated with the Calcutta Chronicle. Dayanand Saraswati wrote the famous work 'Satyarth Prakash'. E. V. Ramaswamy Naicker (Periyar Ramaswami Naicker) was a leader of the Dravidian movement and the 'Self-Respect Movement' in South India, and later joined the Justice Party. **Q69.** With reference to the British Colonial rule in India, consider the following statements : 1. Mahatma Gandhi was instrumental in the abolition of the system of 'indentured labour'. 2. In Lord Chelmsford's 'War Conference', Mahatma Gandhi did not support the resolution on recruiting Indians for World War. 3. Consequent to the breaking of Salt Law by Indian people, the Indian National Congress was declared illegal by the colonial rulers. Which of the statements given above are correct?

- **A.** 1 and 2 only
- **B.** 1 and 3 only
- **C.** 2 and 3 only
- **D.** 1, 2 and 3

**Answer:** B — 1 and 3 only
**Explanation:** Indentured labourers were those who were taken out of India as labourers for fixed periods in the British colonies. Their condition was like that of bonded labourers. Gandhiji first raised his voice in favour of indentured labourers in South Africa in 1894 AD. In the year 1914 AD, by the Gandhi'sSmuts Agreement, the tax of 3 pounds on these labourers ended. After coming back to India, Gandhi negotiated with Viceroy Lord Chelmsford to end the indentured system and finally in July 1917 AD the indentured system was banned. Thus statement (1) is correct. After Gandhiji's Dandi March and his breaking of salt law on April 6, 1930 AD, Indians across the country started violating the salt law. In response to this, many Congress leaders and Satyagrahis like Jawaharlal Nehru, Mahadev Desai etc. were sent to prison and Indian National Congress was declared illegal by British rule. Thus statement (3) is correct.
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 2019

**Q98.** To establish global peace and cooperation among the peoples, which of the following concepts was introduced by Jawaharlal Nehru?

- **A.** Non-alignment
- **B.** Panchsheel
- **C.** Peaceful coexistence
- **D.** None of these.

**Answer:** A — Non-alignment
**Explanation:** The first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, played a crucial role in setting the national agenda. He introduced the concept of Non-Alignment to establish peace and cooperation among people. The three major objectives of Nehru's foreign policy were to preserve the hard-earned sovereignty, protect territorial integrity and promote rapid economic development. Nehru wished to achieve these objectives through the strategy of Non-Alignment. The roots of Non-Alignment Movement (NAM) goes back to the friendship between three leaders - Yugoslavia's Josip Broz Tito, India's Jawaharlal Nehru, and Egypt's leader Gamal Abdel Nasser. Indonesia's Sukarno and Ghana's Kwame Nkrumah strongly supported them. These five leaders came to be known as the five founders of NAM. The first non-aligned summit was held in Belgrade in 1961.
*Asked in:* 46 B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2004

Operation Vijay was conducted by Indian forces to free Goa from Portuguese control. The armed action which involved the Indian Army, Navy and Air Force was a decisive victory for India, ending approximately 450 years of Portuguese rule in India on 19th of December, 1961 AD.

**Q101.** Which of the following statements is not true for Jawaharlal Nehru?

**Explanation:** The first Prime Minister of India Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru was influenced by socialism, British liberalism and also by the thoughts of Mahatma Gandhi, but he was not influenced by the German Nationalism. His famous books, articles, and speeches showed his socialist views.

**Q103.** Consider the following statements: 1. Lord Mountbatten was the Viceroy when Shimla Conference took place. 2. Indian Navy Revolt, 1946 took place when the Indian sailors in the Royal Indian Navy at Bombay and Karachi rose against the Government. Which one of the statements given above is/are correct?

- **A.** 1 only
- **B.** 2 only
- **C.** Both 1 and 2
- **D.** Neither 1 nor 2

**Answer:** B — 2 only
**Explanation:** Lord Wavell was the Viceroy of India when Shimla Conference took place. Thus, statement 1 is false. One of the most spectacular episodes of the intense revolt against the British Raj was the uprising of the sailors of the British Indian Navy in 1946 AD. On February, 18 the sailors and shipmen of the Royal Indian Navy battleship 'HMIS Talwaar,' who were at the time posted to the Bombay harbour, went on strike. They were protesting against the bad food and adverse conditions. After the assurance of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel On 24 February, 1946 AD, the rebels were ready to surrender. Thus, statement 2 is correct.
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 2005

**Q104.** Consider the following statements: 1. Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar founded the Bethune School at Calcutta with the main aim of encouraging education for women. 2. Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay was the first graduate of the Calcutta University. 3. Keshav Chandra Sen's campaign against sati led to the enactment of law to ban sati by the then Governor-General. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

- **A.** 1 only
- **B.** 1 and 2
- **C.** 2 and 3
- **D.** 1, 2 and 3

**Answer:** B — 1 and 2
**Explanation:** Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar encouraged women's education and opened 35 women's schools in Bengal. Pandit Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was the first secretary of Bethune School and its management committee was formed under his chairmanship. Thus statement 1 is correct. The famous Bengali novelist, Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay was one of the first two graduates from Calcutta University in 1858. Thus, statement 2 is also correct. Due to the campaign of Raja Ram Mohan Roy against Sati system, Governor-General Lord William Bentinck banned the Sati system by The Bengal Sati Regulation, 1929. Thus, statement 3 is incorrect and the desired answer will be option (b).
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 2005

Dayanand Saraswati founded Arya Samaj in April 1875 in Bombay with the objective of re-establishing the ancient Vedic religion in pure forms.

**Q133.** Consider the following events and arrange them in correct chronological order. 1. Poona Pact 2. End of Civil Disobedience Movement 3. Gandhi-Irwin Pact 4. Second Round Table Conference Select the correct answer from the code given below : Code :

- **A.** 3, 4, 2, 1
- **B.** 4, 3, 1, 2
- **C.** 4, 3, 2, 1
- **D.** 3, 4, 1, 2

**Answer:** D — 3, 4, 1, 2
**Explanation:** The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on 5 March 1931. The pact opened the way for participation of Congress/ Gandhi in the Second Round Table Conference, which was held in London from September to December 1931. The Poona Pact was concluded on 24 September 1932, under which, in place of a separate electorate for the "Untouchables/ Dalits," the provision of a joint electorate with reserved seats was decided. The Civil Disobedience Movement is formally considered to have ended at the A. I.C.C. Patna session held on 18-19 May 1934. Therefore, the correct sequence is 3 → 4 → 1 → 2, i. e., option (d) is the correct answer.
*Asked in:* U.P. P.C.S (Pre) 2025

**Q135.** Consider the following events and arrange them in chronological order : 1. Linlithgow August Offer 2. Arrival of the Cripps Mission in India 3. Ramgarh Congress Session 4. Resignation of Congress Ministers Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

- **A.** 3, 1, 4, 2
- **B.** 4, 3, 1, 2
- **C.** 1, 3, 4, 2
- **D.** 4, 2, 3, 1

**Answer:** B — 4, 3, 1, 2
**Explanation:** During the Second World War, in protest against Britain's inclusion of India in the war without Indian consent, Congress ministers resigned in October 1939 AD. Subsequently, the 53rd session of the Congress was held in March 1940 AD at Ramgarh (present-day Jharkhand), presided over by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad. In August 1940 AD, the British government introduced the "August Offer" (or Linlithgow offer) to seek Indian support for the war. Later, in 1942 AD, the Cripps Mission was sent to India. This mission proposed limited self-governance for India and was part of a series of efforts to secure Indian cooperation in the war effort.
*Asked in:* U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2024

**Q160.** Match List I with List II List-I List-II Event/Organisation Related Person A. Champaran 1. Jayaprakash Narayan Satyagrah B. Azad Dasta 2. Shyam Narayan Singh C. Individual 3. Sahajanand Saraswati Satyagrah in Bihar 1940 D. Kisan Sabha Bihar 4. Dr. Rajendra Prasad Select the correct answer using the codes given be- low: A B C D

- **A.** 4 2 3 1
- **B.** 2 3 1 4
- **C.** 1 4 3 2
- **D.** 4 1 2 3

**Answer:** D — 4 1 2 3
**Explanation:** The Champaran Satyagraha (1917) was Mahatma Gandhi's first Satyagraha in India, conducted in Bihar on the issue of the problems of Champaran's indigo farmers. Lok Nayak Jayaprakash Narayan organised an armed group for guerrilla action against British rule in the Nepal Terai and Bihar region, which was called the 'Azad Dasta'. Shyam Narayan Singh was among the leading activists from Bihar who undertook the Individual Satyagraha. Swami Sahajanand Saraswati founded the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha and became its widely accepted leader. Later, this movement expanded in the form of the All India Kisan Sabha.
*Asked in:* 71st B.P.S.C. (Pre) 2025

**Q161.** In which chronological order the following events took place ? i. Chauri-Chaura Episode ii. Jallianwala Bagh Massacre iii. Rowlatt Satyagraha iv. Champaran Satyagraha Code :

- **A.** i ii iii iv
- **B.** ii iii iv i
- **C.** iv iii ii i
- **D.** iii ii iv i

**Answer:** C — iv iii ii i
**Explanation:** Gandhi, the exponent of the Satyagraha Movement, staged his first Satyagraha in Champaran, Bihar (in 1917). In the Champaran of Bihar, the cultivators were forced by Europeans to grow indigo, a blue dye and this imposed on them untold sufferings. They could not grow the food they needed, nor did they receive adequate payment for the indigo. Gandhi decided to start his first Satyagraha for the cause of the peasants. Rowlatt Act was passed in March, 1919 by the British Government while Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on April 13,1919 AD in which British troops fired on a large crowd of unarmed Indians in Amritsar in the Punjab of India, killing nearly thousand people and wounding many hundreds more. The Chauri-Chaura episode took place on February 4, 1922 AD, just after this incident, Mahatma Gandhi suspended the Non-Cooperation Movement.
*Asked in:* U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2004

**Explanation:** Montague announced August Declaration on 20 August, 1917, for future policies of British India in reference to India. August Offer was stated by Lord Linlithgow, Viceroy of India on 8 August 1940 regarding the proposal of Congress passed about World War II. Mahatma Gandhi by August Resolution (with the slogan of 'do or die') in 1942 declared to begin the 'Quit India Movement' (also known as 'August Revolution'). Muslim League was not satisfied with the recommendations of Cabinet Mission, so League called 16 August, 1946 as Direct Action Day for the demand of establishment of sovereign & independent state of Pakistan. The main purpose of the League was to spread communal riots.
*Asked in:* U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1997

**Q175.** Consider the following events and arrange them in the correct chronological order, from the earliest to the latest: 1. Royal Indian Navy Revolt 2. Announcement of the Cabinet Mission 3. Formation of the Interim Government 4. Arrival of the UK Parliamentary Delegation in Delhi Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

- **A.** 4, 3, 2, 1
- **B.** 4, 1, 2, 3
- **C.** 4, 2, 1, 3
- **D.** 2, 4, 1, 3

**Answer:** B — 4, 1, 2, 3
**Explanation:** The arrival of the British Parliamentary Delegation in Delhi took place in January 1946 AD. This delegation met prominent Indian leaders and understood their views on independence. The Royal Indian Navy Revolt occurred in February 1946 AD, followed by the arrival of the Cabinet Mission in India on 24 March 1946 AD. On 24 August 1946 AD, under the leadership of Pandit Nehru, the announcement of India's first Interim National Government was made, and its formation took place on 2 September 1946 AD. Thus, the correct chronological order is 4, 1, 2, 3.
*Asked in:* U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2024

**Q225.** Consider the following events during India's freedom struggle: 1. Chauri-Chaura Outrage 2. Minto-Morley Reforms 3. Dandi March 4. Montague-Chelmsford Reforms Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the events above?

**Q226.** The Trade Disputes Act of 1929 provided for :

- **A.** the participation of workers in the management of industries.
- **B.** arbitrary powers to the management to quell industrial disputes.
- **C.** an intervention by the British Court in the event of a trade dispute.
- **D.** a system of tribunals and a ban on strikes.

**Answer:** D — a system of tribunals and a ban on strikes.
**Explanation:** The Trade Dispute Act of 1929 was implemented on an experimental basis for five years. By this Act, provision was made for the formation of Board of Conciliation and Court of Inquiry for investigation and settlement of trade disputes. Strike or lock-out of publicly useful services such as railways, post, telegraph and telephone without prior notice was been prohibited by the act.
*Asked in:* U.P.S.C. CSE (Pre) 2017

**Q227.** Match the List-I with List-II and select the correct answer by using codes given below:- A. Indian Council 1. Beginning of Dyarchy Act, 1909 System B. - **A.** 1 2 3 4
- **B.** 4 3 2 1
- **C.** 2 4 1 3
- **D.** 3 4 2 1

**Answer:** D — 3 4 2 1

So option (d) is correctly matched.

**Q235.** Arrange the following events in their chronological order and select the correct answer by using the codes given at the end: 1. Decision for partition of Bengal. 2. Acceptance of Swaraj as the goal of Congress. 3. Formal declaration of Swadeshi Movement. 4. Surat Split.

- **C.** 1, 2, 3 and 4
- **D.** 1, 2, 4 and 3

**Answer:** B — 1, 3, 2 and 4
**Explanation:** The partition of Bengal was declared on July 20, 1905. The official declaration of Swadeshi Movement was announced on August 7, 1905 at a conference held at Town Hall, Calcutta. Indian National Congress took a positive step in its Calcutta Session regarding the national movement. In his presidential speech, Dadabhai Naoroji said that the main aim of the Indian National Congress was to establish its own Government just like Britain and its dominion. **Q236.** Consider : Assertion(A) : Nehru had no reverence towards Upanishads. Reason(R) : He has a scientific point of view. Select answer by codes given below-

**Q243.** Consider the following statements: 1. Jawaharlal Nehru was in his fourth term as the Prime Minister of India at the time of his death. 2. Jawaharlal Nehru represented Rae Bareilly constituency as a Member of Parliament. 3. The first Non-Congress Prime Minister of India assumed the office in the year 1977. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

- **A.** 1 and 2
- **B.** 3 only
- **C.** 1 only
- **D.** 1 and 3

**Answer:** D — 1 and 3
**Explanation:** Jawaharlal Nehru became Prime Minister in 1947 for first term followed by an election in 1952 for a 2nd term. The election took place in 1957 and he became Prime Minister for a 3rd term and finally after winning 1962 elections, he became Prime Minister for the 4th term and he died in 1964. He never represented Raebareli instead he represented Phulpur constituency near Prayagraj in Uttar Pradesh. From March 24, 1977 Morarji Desai served as Prime Minister as head of a Multiparty front, Janta Party, India's first Non-Congress Government, So, statement (1) and (3) is correct. Hence, the correct answer is option (d).
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 2007

**Q244.** Arrange the following events in correct chronological order: (i) Lucknow Pact (ii) Gandhi-Irwin Pact (iii) Poona Pact (iv) Final Withdrawal of Civil Disobedience Movement Select the correct answer from the codes given below:

- **A.** (i) (iii) (ii) (iv)
- **B.** (i) (ii) (iii) (iv)
- **C.** (i) (iii) (iv) (ii)
- **D.** (i) (iv) (iii) (ii)

**Answer:** B — (i) (ii) (iii) (iv)
**Explanation:** Lucknow Pact - In 1916 during Lucknow Session, an agreement between Congress and Muslim League was settled which is known as Lucknow Pact. It was chaired by Ambica Charan Majumdar. Gandhi-Irwin Pact - The pact signed between Mahatma Gandhi and Lord Irwin on March 5, 1931 is known as GandhiIrwin Pact. In this pact, Gandhi represented Indian National Congress and Irwin represented British Government. The pact is also known as Delhi pact. Poona Pact - The Poona Pact was an agreement between Mahatma Gandhi and B. R. Ambedkar signed on 24 September, 1932 by the efforts of Madan Mohan Malviya C. Rajagopalachari, Rajendra Prasad and Purushottamdas. Final Withdrawal of Civil Disobedience Movement - On August 1, 1934 Gandhi started Individual Civil Disobedience Movement, but his movement was unsuccessful due to its short and disappointing nature.
*Asked in:* U.P.P.C.S. (Spl.) (Pre) 2008

**Q249.** Arrange the following post-independence events in chronological order : 1. Liberation of Goa 2. Dalai Lama fled to India 3. Chou-en-Lai visited India 4. India visit of Khrushchev and Bulganin Select the correct answer the code given below:

**Q258.** The objective of the Butler Committee of 1927 was to :

- **A.** Define the jurisdiction of the Central and Provincial Governments.
- **B.** Define the powers of the Secretary of State for India.
- **C.** Impose censorship of the national press.
- **D.** Improve the relationship between the Government of India and the Indian States.

**Answer:** D — Improve the relationship between the Government of India and the Indian States.
**Explanation:** The Indian State Committee constituted a committee in the year 1927 under the Chairmanship of Sir Harcourt Butler, also known as the Butler Committee. The formation of this Committee was about the investigation and classification of relationship between the Supreme power and the Native kings. The Committee visited 16 states and submitted its report in the year 1929. After examining the existing relations of Supreme (British) power in Indian and princely states the Committee presented its recommendations regarding the financial and economic relation of these two.
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 2017

**Q259.** When was the special rights and privy purse enjoyed by the Indian Princely States abolished?

- **A.** 1950
- **B.** 1949
- **C.** 1962
- **D.** 1971

**Answer:** D — 1971
**Explanation:** Privy purse was a payment made to erstwhile Indian princely states' ruling families by central government of India as part of their agreement to merge their states with the Republic of India in 1949 thereby ending their ruling rights. However all the special rights and privy purse enjoyed by Indian Princely States were abolished by 26th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1971 in the year of 1971.
*Asked in:* M.P.P.C.S. (Pre.) 2020

**Q261.** Who among the following were the founders of the "Hind Mazdoor Sabha" established in 1948?

- **A.** B. Krishna Pillai, E.M.S. Namboodiripad and K.C. George
- **B.** Jayaprakash Narayan, Deen Dayal Upadhyay and M.N. Roy
- **C.** C.P. Ramaswamy Iyer, K. Kamaraj and Veeresalingam Pantulu
- **D.** Ashok Mehta, T.S. Ramanujam and G.G. Mehta

**Answer:** D — Ashok Mehta, T.S. Ramanujam and G.G. Mehta
**Explanation:** Hind Mazdoor Sabha (HMS) was established during a trade union conference held in Calcutta in December, 1948. In this Indian Federation of Labour (estd. 1941), Hind Mazdoor Panchayat (HMP, estd 1948), unions of Forward Block and top most independent business unions also participated. During the founding conference Ramachandra Sakharam Ruikar was elected as first President and Ashok Mehta as General Secretary, G. G. Mehta and V. S. Mathur were selected as secretary. Maniben Kara and T. S. Ramanujan were chosen as Vice Presidents of HMS and R. A. Khedagikar was selected as treasurer.
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 2018

**Q266.** Karl Marx explained the process of class struggle with the help of which one of the following theories?

- **A.** Empirical liberalism
- **B.** Existentialism
- **C.** Darwin's theory of evolution
- **D.** Dialectical materialism

**Answer:** D — Dialectical materialism
**Explanation:** Karl Marx explained the process of class struggle with the help of dialectical materialism. According to Marx, in the process of historical chronology, "Slavery" was the base of ancient society. "Land" was the base of Feudal Society and "Capital" was the base of middle-class society. It is his "Materialistic description of History" According to Marx, the history of society is determined by economic causes that inherit class struggle.
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 2011

**Answer:** A — Unhappy India - Bal Gangadhar Tilak
**Explanation:** Lieutenant-Colonel James Tod, in his book 'Annals and Antiquities of Rajasthan' wrote about 'Feudalism' in Rajasthan. Option (a) is not correctly matched. The author of 'Unhappy India' is Lala Lajpat Rai, not Bal Gangadhar Tilak who chaired the Special Session of Indian National Congress (1920). Bal Gangadhar Tilak edited 'Kesari' and 'The Mahratta'. Bankimchandra Chatterjee, was the author of 'Durgesh Nandini' who also wrote 'Anandmath'. 'India Wins Freedom' was written by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad. The Book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' was written by Dadabhai Naoroji.

**Q80.** With reference to the book "Desher Katha" written by Sakharam Ganesh Deuskar during the freedom struggle, consider the following statements: 1. It warned against the Colonial State's hypnotic conquest of the mind. 2. It inspired the performance of Swadeshi street plays and folk songs. 3. The use of 'desh' by Deuskar was in the specific context of the region of Bengal. Which of the statements given above are correct?

- **A.** 1 and 2 only
- **B.** 2 and 3 only
- **C.** 1 and 3 only
- **D.** 1, 2 and 3

**Answer:** A — 1 and 2 only
**Explanation:** Sakharam Ganesh Deuskar was a bridge between the Renaissance of Maharashtra and Bengal. Maharashtra was his inspiration but he wrote in Bengali. He wrote "Desher Katha", which was inspired by the ideas of Naoroji and Ranade. In his book he warned against the Colonial State's hypnotic conquest of the mind. It inspired Swadeshi street plays and folk songs, and acquired a cult status among Swadeshi activists. Deuskar used desh to mean nation in the text.

**Q111.** The song 'Amar Sonar Bangla' written during the Swadeshi Movement of India inspired the liberation struggle of Bangladesh and was adopted as the National Anthem of Bangladesh. Who wrote this song?

- **A.** Rajni Kanta Sen
- **B.** Dwijendralal Roy
- **C.** Mukunda Das
- **D.** Rabindranath Tagore

**Answer:** D — Rabindranath Tagore
**Explanation:** The song 'Amar Sonar Bangla' was written and composed by Rabindranath Tagore during the Bengal partition movement of 1905. The music of this song is inspired by the melody of the Hymn 'Ami Kothay Pabo Tare' written by Gagan Harkara. Bangladesh adopted the first 10 lines of this song as its National Anthem. Syed Ali Ahsan translated the song into English. It is noteworthy that Rabindranath Tagore wrote the National Anthem of India 'Jana Gana Mana'. He is the only poet in the world whose compositions have been adopted as the national anthem of the two countries.
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 2007

Syed Ali Ahsan translated the song into English. It is noteworthy that Rabindranath Tagore wrote the National Anthem of India 'Jana Gana Mana'. He is the only poet in the world whose compositions have been adopted as the national anthem of the two countries.

## 54. Art and Culture

**Q1.** The first Gandharva Mahavidyalaya, a music training school, was set up in 1901 by Vishnu Digambar Paluskar in

- **A.** Delhi
- **B.** Gwalior
- **C.** Ujjain
- **D.** Lahore

**Answer:** D — Lahore
**Explanation:** Gandharva Mahavidyalaya was one of the earliest institutions established for the organized training in classical music through a modern method. Pandit Vishnu Digambar Paluskar founded the first Gandharva Mahavidyalaya in Lahore in 1901, which was then a part of undivided India. Paluskar sought to take music education out of the exclusive hereditary domain of professional musicians and make it accessible to the wider public.
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 2025

**Q2.** Consider the following pairs: (Tradition) (State) 1. Gatka, a traditional - Kerala martial art 2. Madhubani, a traditional - Bihar painting 3. Singhey Khababs - Jammu and Kashmir Sindhu Darshan festival Which of the above pair (s) is/are correctly matched?

- **A.** 1 and 2
- **B.** 3 only
- **C.** 2 and 3
- **D.** 1, 2 and 3

Madhubani painting or Mithila painting is a unique style of painting, practiced in the Mithila region of Nepal and Indian state of Bihar. Singhey-Khababs Sindhu Darshan Festival is a Festival of India held every year in the month of June. It is held at Leh, in Ladakh U. T. (which was part of J&K at time when question was asked)
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 2009

**Q5.** In the context of the cultural history of India, a pose in dance and dramatics called Tribhanga has been a favourite of Indian artists from ancient times till today. Which one of the following statements best describes this pose?

- **A.** One leg is bent and the body is slightly but oppositely curved at waist and neck
- **B.** Facial expressions, hand gestures and make-up are combined to symbolize certain epic or historical characters
- **C.** Movements of body, face and hands are used to express oneself or to tell a story
- **D.** A little smile, slightly curved waist and certain hand gestures are emphasized to express the feelings of love or eroticism.

**Answer:** A — One leg is bent and the body is slightly but oppositely curved at waist and neck
**Explanation:** Tribhanga (tri-bent pose) is a standing body position or stance used in the traditional Indian sculpture, art and Indian classical dance forms. Tribhanga is literally means three parts break, consisting of three bends in the body; at the neck, waist and knee which gives it a gentle 'S' shape. Hence option (a) is the correct answer.
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 2013

**Q6.** Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R): Assertion (A) : For education and culture a Centre for Cultural Resources and Training (CCRT) was set up in 1979. Reason (R) : The objective of CCRT was to link education with culture. Choose the correct answer from the codes given below. Codes:

- **A.** Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
- **B.** Both A and R are true and R is not the correct explanation of A
- **C.** A is true but R is false
- **D.** A is false but R is true

**Answer:** A — Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
**Explanation:** Centre for Cultural Resources and Training (CCRT) is a premier institution working in the field of linking education with culture. It was established in 1979, by Smt. Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay and Dr. Kapila Vatsyayan. It functions as an autonomous organisation under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India. CCRT's commitment lies to holistic education, encompassing the cognitive, emotional and spiritual development of children. Hence it is clear that both A and R are correct and R is correct explanation of A.
*Asked in:* U.P.R.O./A.R.O. (Pre) (Re-Exam) 2016

**Q7.** At which of the following places Kumbh Mela is not held?

- **A.** Nashik
- **B.** Haridwar
- **C.** Prayag
- **D.** Varanasi

**Answer:** D — Varanasi
**Explanation:** Kumbh Mela is a mass Hindu pilgrimage of faith in which Hindus gather to take a dip in a holy river. It is the world's largest religious gathering. It is held every third year at one of the four places by rotation: Haridwar, Prayagraj, Nashik and Ujjain. Thus the Kumbh Mela is held at each of these four places every twelfth year. However, U. P. government has changed the name of Kumbh mela (every 12 years) to Mahakumbh and Ardh Kumbh mela (every 6 years) to Kumbh (at Prayagraj).
*Asked in:* M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 1992

P. government has changed the name of Kumbh Mela (every 12 years) to Mahakumbh and Ardh Kumbh Mela (every 6 years) to Kumbh (at Prayagraj).
*Asked in:* M.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2013

**Q19.** Four Mathas established by Adi Shankaracharya are :

- **A.** Joshimath, Dwarka, Puri, Sringeri
- **B.** Sringeri, Dwarka, Joshimath, Prayag
- **C.** Dwarka, Joshimath, Prayag, Kanchi
- **D.** Puri, Sringeri, Dwarka, Varanasi

**Answer:** A — Joshimath, Dwarka, Puri, Sringeri
**Explanation:** Adi Shankaracharya was one of the most notable philosophers as well as savants of India. He established four Peethas or Mathas in the four corners of India. The four Mathas established by him are- Jyotirmath or Joshimath in the north, Govardhan Math in Puri in the east, Dwarka Sharda Peeth in Dwarka in the west and Sringeri Sharada Peetham in Sringeri in the south.

**Q48.** With reference to Dhrupad, one of the major traditions of India that has been kept alive for centuries, which of the following statements are correct? 1. Dhrupad originated and developed in the Rajput kingdoms during the Mughal period. 2. Dhrupad is primarily a devotional and spiritual music. 3. Dhrupad Alap uses Sanskrit syllables from Mantras. Select the correct answer using the codes given below:

- **A.** 1 and 2
- **B.** 2 and 3
- **C.** 1, 2 and 3
- **D.** None of these

**Answer:** B — 2 and 3
**Explanation:** Dhrupad is the Indian classical music that traces its origin to the chanting of Vedic hymns and mantras. It was originated by King of Gwalior Man Singh Tomar (1486-1516). Hence, Dhrupad was originated way back before Mughal Period. Hence statement 1 is wrong. It is also primarily a form of worship, in which offerings are made to the divine through sound. Thus Statement 2 is correct. Dhrupad is performed in two parts- Alap and Bandish. In the Alap, the singer uses syllables from Sanskrit Mantras. Therefore, statement 3 is correct.
*Asked in:* I.A.S. (Pre) 2012

**Q53.** With reference to Manipuri Sankirtana, consider the following statements: 1. It is a song and dance performance. 2. Cymbals are the only musical instruments used in the performance. 3. It is performed to narrate the life and deeds of Lord Krishna. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

- **A.** 1, 2 and 3
- **B.** 1 and 3 only
- **C.** 2 and 3 only
- **D.** 1 only

**Answer:** B — 1 and 3 only
**Explanation:** Manipuri Sankirtana is one of the few important Indian heritage inscribed on the UNESCO representative list of the intangible cultural heritage of humanity. It is a form of performing art involving virtual singing, drumming and dancing which are performed in the temples and domestic spaces in Manipur state. Through the performances which exhibit unparalleled religious devotion and energy, the performers narrates the life and deeds of Lord Krishna. So, statements 1 and 3 are correct. Since the Kartal and Pung are also used, statement 2 is incorrect.
